919:### 6.6 Processes (plugin)
920:
921:#### Process RunStatelessInvocation: run a stateless invocation (plugin process) [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-009]
922:
923:- Not a unit of work: the plugin orchestrates the handlers GetAgentContextStatusQuery (status), BuildAgentContextPackageCommand (build), SubmitAgentResponseCommand (submit), and RunDeterministicGradeCommand (deterministic grade) through the REPL.
924:- Trigger: a delivered user request (Phase A processes ApplyArrivalBridgeRecord and OpenTurnFromPromptHook) on a host whose plugin reads `Mode` through GetAgentContextStatusQuery.
925:- PowerShell core: `Invoke-PluginAgentContextInvocation` in `plugin-hook.ps1`, for all nine hosts (the TypeScript hosts through their adapters). Hosts inject the rendered package through their prompt-context mechanism (hook additional context or the host's system-context API).
926:- Output: in `Stateless` mode the model receives only the rendered package and the request, without prior conversation turns; in `Pilot` mode the package is built and recorded but not injected; in `Off` nothing happens.
927:- Package failure (operator, 2026-10-11: "Fail the invocation"): in `Pilot` or `Stateless` mode, when the build fails (budget overflow, profile unavailable, commit unavailable, any other error, or an outage), the plugin refuses the prompt with the error code and message shown to the operator, produces no answer, and closes the request's turn `canceled` with that reason (canceled turns are not gated, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002). This is the only `canceled` a hook ever writes, and only for the failed request's own turn, never another turn (the Phase A isolation rule, refined for this case: `Isolation_HooksNeverPersistCanceled_ExceptOwnTurnPackageFailure`); the plugin removes the request from `openDelivered` and the Stop ledger only after the server confirms the close, so the Stop gate never waits on a turn the plugin itself closed (`StatelessPackageFailure_ClosesOwnTurnCanceled_RemovedFromLedger_NoOtherTurnTouched`). A host whose prompt hook cannot refuse a prompt cannot run `Pilot` or `Stateless`; its plugin treats those modes as `Off` and its feature-matrix row records the limitation.
928:- History exclusion (operator: "Each agent invocation can run stateless"): in `Stateless` mode the model's input for the request is exactly the rendered package plus the current request. The plugin achieves it only through an authoritative host operation recorded in the host's P0.2 row: replacing the model's message list for that request (opencode `experimental.chat.messages.transform`, whose `output.messages` the adapter replaces with the list the core returns) or starting a fresh host invocation whose only input is the package and the request. A host without such an operation cannot run `Stateless`: its plugin treats `Stateless` as `Pilot` (the package is built and recorded, the model answers statefully) and its feature-matrix row records the limitation (`Stateless_HostWithoutHistoryExclusion_TreatedAsPilot_FeatureMatrixRow`). Each supported host has a host-level test that sends a sentinel prior turn and asserts, on the model request the host actually sends (recorded by the adapter fixture), that the sentinel is absent while the package and the current request are present (`StatelessHost_SentinelPriorTurn_AbsentFromModelRequest`).
929:- A host recorded `turn_logging_unsupported` (Phase A, D6) has no minted turn, so RunStatelessInvocation does not run there: the plugin stays stateful and reports `turn_logging_unsupported`.
930:- After the model answers, the response is submitted (SubmitAgentResponseCommand) at turn close and graded deterministically (RunDeterministicGradeCommand); its model grade comes later from an HV request covering its turn (CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand).
931:
932:```mermaid
933:flowchart TD
934:    S(["Request delivered"]) --> SUP{"Host supported for turn logging and the turn minted?"}
935:    SUP -->|no| UNS(["turn_logging_unsupported: stateful, no package"])
936:    SUP -->|yes| MD["Read Mode from status (cached per host session start)"]
937:    MD --> M{"Mode"}
938:    M -->|Off| OFF(["Stateful turn as today"])
939:    M -->|Pilot or Stateless| CAN{"Host prompt hook can refuse a prompt?"}
940:    CAN -->|no| LIM(["Treated as Off: stateful, limitation in the feature matrix"])
941:    CAN -->|yes| BP["Build package (BuildAgentContextPackageCommand) for sessionId and requestId, idempotency key = requestId"]
942:    BP --> BR{"Build result"}
943:    BR -->|any error or outage| REF["Refuse the prompt with the error code and message shown to the operator"]
944:    REF --> CN["Close this request's own turn canceled with the reason; after the server confirms, remove it from openDelivered and the Stop ledger"]
945:    CN --> FAIL(["Invocation failed: no answer produced"])
946:    BR -->|built| MM{"Mode"}
947:    MM -->|Pilot| PIL["Record packageId on the turn, no injection"]
948:    PIL --> RUN1["Model answers statefully"]
949:    MM -->|Stateless| HX{"Host has an authoritative history-exclusion operation (P0.2 row)?"}
950:    HX -->|no| PIL
951:    HX -->|yes| INJ["Replace the model input with the rendered package and the request (message-list replacement or fresh invocation): no history reaches the model"]
952:    INJ --> RUN2["Model answers from the package"]
953:    RUN1 --> SUB["At turn close submit the response (SubmitAgentResponseCommand) with claims, evidence, and invocationMode"]
954:    RUN2 --> SUB
955:    SUB --> SR{"Submit result"}
956:    SR -->|201 or 200| GRD["Deterministic grade (RunDeterministicGradeCommand)"]
957:    SR -->|error or outage| SE["Record the cause on the turn, keep the turn open for the Stop gate"]
958:    SE --> E3(["Response not recorded: the model or operator resubmits"])
959:    GRD --> GDR{"Grade result"}
960:    GDR -->|201| WAIT(["Response Grading until an HV request covering the turn records its model grade (CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand)"])
961:    GDR -->|error| GE(["Cause recorded on the turn: the deterministic grade is re-run on request"])

919:### 6.6 Processes (plugin)
920:
921:#### Process RunStatelessInvocation: run a stateless invocation (plugin process) [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-009]
922:
923:- Not a unit of work: the plugin orchestrates the handlers GetAgentContextStatusQuery (status), BuildAgentContextPackageCommand (build), SubmitAgentResponseCommand (submit), and RunDeterministicGradeCommand (deterministic grade) through the REPL.
924:- Trigger: a delivered user request (Phase A processes ApplyArrivalBridgeRecord and OpenTurnFromPromptHook) on a host whose plugin reads `Mode` through GetAgentContextStatusQuery.
925:- PowerShell core: `Invoke-PluginAgentContextInvocation` in `plugin-hook.ps1`, for all nine hosts (the TypeScript hosts through their adapters). Hosts inject the rendered package through their prompt-context mechanism (hook additional context or the host's system-context API).
926:- Output: in `Stateless` mode the model receives only the rendered package and the request, without prior conversation turns; in `Pilot` mode the package is built and recorded but not injected; in `Off` nothing happens.
927:- Package failure (operator, 2026-10-11: "Fail the invocation"): in `Pilot` or `Stateless` mode, when the build fails (budget overflow, profile unavailable, commit unavailable, any other error, or an outage), the plugin refuses the prompt with the error code and message shown to the operator, produces no answer, and closes the request's turn `canceled` with that reason (canceled turns are not gated, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002). This is the only `canceled` a hook ever writes, and only for the failed request's own turn, never another turn (the Phase A isolation rule, refined for this case: `Isolation_HooksNeverPersistCanceled_ExceptOwnTurnPackageFailure`); the plugin removes the request from `openDelivered` and the Stop ledger only after the server confirms the close, so the Stop gate never waits on a turn the plugin itself closed (`StatelessPackageFailure_ClosesOwnTurnCanceled_RemovedFromLedger_NoOtherTurnTouched`). A host whose prompt hook cannot refuse a prompt cannot run `Pilot` or `Stateless`; its plugin treats those modes as `Off` and its feature-matrix row records the limitation.
928:- History exclusion (operator: "Each agent invocation can run stateless"): in `Stateless` mode the model's input for the request is exactly the rendered package plus the current request. The plugin achieves it only through an authoritative host operation recorded in the host's P0.2 row: replacing the model's message list for that request (opencode `experimental.chat.messages.transform`, whose `output.messages` the adapter replaces with the list the core returns) or starting a fresh host invocation whose only input is the package and the request. A host without such an operation cannot run `Stateless`: its plugin treats `Stateless` as `Pilot` (the package is built and recorded, the model answers statefully) and its feature-matrix row records the limitation (`Stateless_HostWithoutHistoryExclusion_TreatedAsPilot_FeatureMatrixRow`). Each supported host has a host-level test that sends a sentinel prior turn and asserts, on the model request the host actually sends (recorded by the adapter fixture), that the sentinel is absent while the package and the current request are present (`StatelessHost_SentinelPriorTurn_AbsentFromModelRequest`).
929:- A host recorded `turn_logging_unsupported` (Phase A, D6) has no minted turn, so RunStatelessInvocation does not run there: the plugin stays stateful and reports `turn_logging_unsupported`.
930:- After the model answers, the response is submitted (SubmitAgentResponseCommand) at turn close and graded deterministically (RunDeterministicGradeCommand); its model grade comes later from an HV request covering its turn (CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand).

1696:## 7. Agent-context use cases
1697:
1698:### 7.11 Use case: Build a context package for a request [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001, -002]
1699:
1700:Actors: agent host and plugin, server. Precondition: the request's turn exists (UC-1) and the mode is `Pilot` or `Stateless`. Basic flow: the plugin asks the server to build a package for the request; the server gathers the request, profile, rules, applicable requirements, related turns, TODOs, receipts, trusted prior responses, and code at the current commit, filters secrets and untrusted items, ranks, fills the budget, records provenance, and returns the rendered package. Alternate flows: mandatory context exceeds the budget and the build fails with `agent_context_budget_exceeded`; the same idempotency key returns the same package; the commit is unreadable; replay proves the package is reproducible.
1701:
1702:```mermaid
1703:flowchart LR
1704:    HO(["Agent host and plugin"]) --- U(("Build a context package (BuildAgentContextPackageCommand)"))
1705:    SV(["Server"]) --- U
1706:    U -. include .-> I1(("Retrieve candidates (RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery)"))
1707:    U -. include .-> I2(("Record provenance, omissions, findings"))
1708:    E1(("Mandatory over budget: 422, invocation fails")) -. extend .-> U
1709:    E2(("Repeated key: same package")) -. extend .-> U
1710:    E3(("Replay proves determinism (ReplayAgentContextPackageQuery)")) -. extend .-> U
1711:```
1712:
1713:### 7.12 Use case: Submit and grade an agent response [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-003, -004]
1714:
1715:Actors: model, plugin, server, hostile reviewer. Basic flow: at turn close the plugin submits the model's response with its claims and evidence; the server runs the deterministic grade; an agent creates an HV request covering the turn (CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand) and the HV agent records the model grade (RecordModelGradeCommand) after the receipt and reviewer checks; the server marks the response trusted when both grades pass at 98/98 with zero FAIL and zero UNKNOWN. Alternate flows: a grade fails and the response stays `Grading` with every failure shown; a grader other than the configured one is refused; the operator rejects the response.
1716:
1717:```mermaid
1718:flowchart LR
1719:    MD(["Model"]) --- U(("Submit and grade a response"))
1720:    PL(["Plugin"]) --- U
1721:    HR(["Hostile reviewer"]) --- U
1722:    SV(["Server"]) --- U
1723:    U -. include .-> I1(("Submit (SubmitAgentResponseCommand)"))
1724:    U -. include .-> I2(("Deterministic grade (RunDeterministicGradeCommand)"))
1725:    U -. include .-> I3(("Model grade (RecordModelGradeCommand)"))
1726:    U -. include .-> I4(("Decide trust (DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand)"))
1727:    E1(("Grade fails: stays Grading, failures shown")) -. extend .-> U
1728:    E2(("Unconfigured grader: 403")) -. extend .-> U
1729:    E3(("Rejected by operator (RejectAgentResponseCommand)")) -. extend .-> U
1730:```
1731:
1732:### 7.13 Use case: Retrieve trusted prior context [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-007]
1733:
1734:Actors: server (inside package construction), client apps. Basic flow: retrieval returns ranked candidates, only trusted responses among prior responses, preferring GraphRAG. Alternate flow: GraphRAG disabled, uninitialized, not indexed, or failing, and the deterministic relational path answers with the fallback reason.
1735:
1736:```mermaid
1737:flowchart LR
1738:    SV(["Server: package builder"]) --- U(("Retrieve trusted prior context (RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery)"))
1739:    CA(["Client apps"]) --- U
1740:    E1(("GraphRAG unavailable: relational fallback with reason")) -. extend .-> U
1741:```
1742:
1743:### 7.14 Use case: Maintain relationships, staleness, and supersession [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-005, -006]
1744:
1745:Actors: model, operator, server. Basic flow: links are created between packages, responses, requirements, turns, TODOs, code, and receipts; when a dependency changes, its dependents become stale; a newer response supersedes an older one. Alternate flows: invalid link, cycle, or unresolvable ref refused.

1748:flowchart LR
1749:    MD(["Model"]) --- U(("Maintain relationships and staleness"))
1750:    OP(["Operator"]) --- U
1751:    SV(["Server"]) --- U
1752:    U -. include .-> I1(("Create, delete, query links (CreateAgentContextRelationshipCommand to QueryAgentContextRelationshipsQuery)"))
1753:    U -. include .-> I2(("Evaluate staleness (EvaluateStalenessCommand)"))
1754:    E1(("Supersede a response (SupersedeAgentResponseCommand)")) -. extend .-> U
1755:    E2(("Invalid link or cycle refused")) -. extend .-> U
1756:```
1757:
1758:### 7.15 Use case: Run a stateless or pilot invocation [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-009]
1759:
1760:Actors: operator, agent host and plugin, model. Basic flow: in `Stateless` mode the plugin builds the package for a delivered request and the model answers from the package alone; in `Pilot` mode the package is built and recorded but the model answers statefully; the pilot report compares both before any default changes. Alternate flows: mode `Off` keeps today's behavior; a build failure (operator, 2026-10-11: "Fail the invocation") refuses the prompt with the error code and message shown to the operator, produces no answer, and closes the turn `canceled`; a host whose prompt hook cannot refuse a prompt treats `Pilot` and `Stateless` as `Off`, with the limitation in its feature-matrix row.

1768:    U -. include .-> I2(("Submit and grade an agent response"))
1769:    E1(("Mode Off: stateful")) -. extend .-> U
1770:    E2(("Build fails: prompt refused, turn canceled")) -. extend .-> U
1771:    E3(("Pilot report (GetAgentContextPilotReportQuery)")) -. extend .-> U

1774:### 7.16 Use case: Project responses into GraphRAG [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-007]
1775:
1776:Actors: server (background pass), operator. Basic flow: trusted responses are ingested into GraphRAG and responses that stop being trusted are removed. Alternate flows: GraphRAG disabled and every projection skipped; an ingest or delete error is recorded and retried on the next pass.

1783:    E2(("Ingest or delete error: Failed, retried")) -. extend .-> U

1787:
1788:### 8.1 Phase order
1789:
1790:```mermaid
1791:flowchart LR
1792:    PRE["Prerequisites: P0.1 baseline, REPL generateDocument fix, Nuke Test parameters, TestPluginCore, TestAgentPlugins, bats cases ported to Pester, Build.Tests out of MigrationIntegrationTests"] --> REQ["Phase 1 Requirements (the plan's P0 steps 1-9): every FR, TR, TEST, AC, mapping, use case, TODO"]
1793:    REQ --> DES["Phase 2 Interfaces and code stubs: every command, query, policy, seam, unregistered entity and configuration class, DTO, surface, plugin signature"]
1794:    DES --> TST["Phase 3 TDD unit tests with mocks: every unit test RED on stubs, then green on mocks with negative checks"]
1795:    TST --> IMP["Phase 4 Implementation: one coding agent per bounded context, in parallel"]
1796:    IMP --> VER["Integration, live checks on Linux and Windows, phase-wide HV, operator approval"]
1797:```
1798:
1799:Each arrow is crossed only after that phase's gates are green with zero failures and zero skips, its hostile validation (Codex gpt-6-astra max) returns AGREE at accuracy and completeness of at least 98 with every claim PASS, and the operator approves.
1800:
1801:### 8.2 What each phase delivers
1802:
1803:- Prerequisites: every pre-existing failure fixed under its own TODO (P0.1, including the Windows findings), the REPL `generateDocument` validator fix, the Nuke targets every later gate runs through (`Test --test-projects --test-filter`, `TestPluginCore`, `TestAgentPlugins`), and the port of every bats case to Pester (P0.1b; Pester is the only plugin test runner, operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."), and Build.Tests removed from `MigrationIntegrationTests` (P0.1c, TR-MCP-NUKE-014).
1804:- Phase 1, requirements (the plan's P0 steps 1-9): the whole catalog of Phases A, B, and C created in the requirement store from the plan text, the use cases, the feature matrix rows, and the phase and domain TODOs (`REQ-MERGEDPLAN-001`, `DESIGN-MERGEDPLAN-001`, `TEST-MERGEDPLAN-001`, one `IMPL-<CONTEXT>-001` per bounded context, `VERIFY-MERGEDPLAN-001`).
1805:- Phase 2, interfaces and code stubs: every command and query record with a handler stub, every policy and seam interface with a stub, every new entity class and its `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` as compiling, unregistered classes (no `DbSet`, no registration in `McpDbContext`, and no new property on an existing entity, because `McpDbContext.cs:301-308` ignores the pending-model-changes warning, so a registered model change without its migration would make queries select columns the database lacks and regress the existing tests that call `Migrate()`; the registered model change, the three migrations, and the S3 backfill belong to the Phase 4 context StorageSchema), every DTO and client mirror with JSON context registration, every controller route, MCP tool, client method, and REPL method (they only dispatch), every plugin function and tool signature, the options classes and `appsettings.yaml` sections, DI, and the golden contract files. Stubs return neutral values and never throw, so Phase 3 tests fail on assertions.
1806:- Phase 3, unit tests with mocks: every unit test the catalog names, written from the acceptance criteria, recorded RED against the stubs, then green against mocks with the oracle and mutant pattern and a recorded negative check each.
1807:- Phase 4, implementation: each bounded context replaces its stubs with the real implementation until its Phase 3 tests pass unchanged, adds its integration tests, and runs its gates; then the contexts merge in the rollout order and the integration gates, live checks, and phase-wide HV run.

1698:### 7.11 Use case: Build a context package for a request [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001, -002]
1699:
1700:Actors: agent host and plugin, server. Precondition: the request's turn exists (UC-1) and the mode is `Pilot` or `Stateless`. Basic flow: the plugin asks the server to build a package for the request; the server gathers the request, profile, rules, applicable requirements, related turns, TODOs, receipts, trusted prior responses, and code at the current commit, filters secrets and untrusted items, ranks, fills the budget, records provenance, and returns the rendered package. Alternate flows: mandatory context exceeds the budget and the build fails with `agent_context_budget_exceeded`; the same idempotency key returns the same package; the commit is unreadable; replay proves the package is reproducible.
1701:
1702:```mermaid
1703:flowchart LR
1704:    HO(["Agent host and plugin"]) --- U(("Build a context package (BuildAgentContextPackageCommand)"))
1705:    SV(["Server"]) --- U
1706:    U -. include .-> I1(("Retrieve candidates (RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery)"))
1707:    U -. include .-> I2(("Record provenance, omissions, findings"))
1708:    E1(("Mandatory over budget: 422, invocation fails")) -. extend .-> U
1709:    E2(("Repeated key: same package")) -. extend .-> U
1710:    E3(("Replay proves determinism (ReplayAgentContextPackageQuery)")) -. extend .-> U
1711:```

1713:### 7.12 Use case: Submit and grade an agent response [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-003, -004]
1714:
1715:Actors: model, plugin, server, hostile reviewer. Basic flow: at turn close the plugin submits the model's response with its claims and evidence; the server runs the deterministic grade; an agent creates an HV request covering the turn (CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand) and the HV agent records the model grade (RecordModelGradeCommand) after the receipt and reviewer checks; the server marks the response trusted when both grades pass at 98/98 with zero FAIL and zero UNKNOWN. Alternate flows: a grade fails and the response stays `Grading` with every failure shown; a grader other than the configured one is refused; the operator rejects the response.

1724:    U -. include .-> I2(("Deterministic grade (RunDeterministicGradeCommand)"))
1725:    U -. include .-> I3(("Model grade (RecordModelGradeCommand)"))
1726:    U -. include .-> I4(("Decide trust (DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand)"))
1727:    E1(("Grade fails: stays Grading, failures shown")) -. extend .-> U
1728:    E2(("Unconfigured grader: 403")) -. extend .-> U
1729:    E3(("Rejected by operator (RejectAgentResponseCommand)")) -. extend .-> U

1758:### 7.15 Use case: Run a stateless or pilot invocation [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-009]
1759:
1760:Actors: operator, agent host and plugin, model. Basic flow: in `Stateless` mode the plugin builds the package for a delivered request and the model answers from the package alone; in `Pilot` mode the package is built and recorded but the model answers statefully; the pilot report compares both before any default changes. Alternate flows: mode `Off` keeps today's behavior; a build failure (operator, 2026-10-11: "Fail the invocation") refuses the prompt with the error code and message shown to the operator, produces no answer, and closes the turn `canceled`; a host whose prompt hook cannot refuse a prompt treats `Pilot` and `Stateless` as `Off`, with the limitation in its feature-matrix row.

1696:## 7. Agent-context use cases
1697:
1698:### 7.11 Use case: Build a context package for a request [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001, -002]
1699:
1700:Actors: agent host and plugin, server. Precondition: the request's turn exists (UC-1) and the mode is `Pilot` or `Stateless`. Basic flow: the plugin asks the server to build a package for the request; the server gathers the request, profile, rules, applicable requirements, related turns, TODOs, receipts, trusted prior responses, and code at the current commit, filters secrets and untrusted items, ranks, fills the budget, records provenance, and returns the rendered package. Alternate flows: mandatory context exceeds the budget and the build fails with `agent_context_budget_exceeded`; the same idempotency key returns the same package; the commit is unreadable; replay proves the package is reproducible.
1701:
1702:```mermaid
1703:flowchart LR
1704:    HO(["Agent host and plugin"]) --- U(("Build a context package (BuildAgentContextPackageCommand)"))
1705:    SV(["Server"]) --- U
1706:    U -. include .-> I1(("Retrieve candidates (RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery)"))
1707:    U -. include .-> I2(("Record provenance, omissions, findings"))
1708:    E1(("Mandatory over budget: 422, invocation fails")) -. extend .-> U
1709:    E2(("Repeated key: same package")) -. extend .-> U
1710:    E3(("Replay proves determinism (ReplayAgentContextPackageQuery)")) -. extend .-> U
1711:```
1712:
1713:### 7.12 Use case: Submit and grade an agent response [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-003, -004]
1714:
1715:Actors: model, plugin, server, hostile reviewer. Basic flow: at turn close the plugin submits the model's response with its claims and evidence; the server runs the deterministic grade; an agent creates an HV request covering the turn (CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand) and the HV agent records the model grade (RecordModelGradeCommand) after the receipt and reviewer checks; the server marks the response trusted when both grades pass at 98/98 with zero FAIL and zero UNKNOWN. Alternate flows: a grade fails and the response stays `Grading` with every failure shown; a grader other than the configured one is refused; the operator rejects the response.
1716:
1717:```mermaid
1718:flowchart LR
1719:    MD(["Model"]) --- U(("Submit and grade a response"))
1720:    PL(["Plugin"]) --- U
1721:    HR(["Hostile reviewer"]) --- U
1722:    SV(["Server"]) --- U
1723:    U -. include .-> I1(("Submit (SubmitAgentResponseCommand)"))
1724:    U -. include .-> I2(("Deterministic grade (RunDeterministicGradeCommand)"))
1725:    U -. include .-> I3(("Model grade (RecordModelGradeCommand)"))
1726:    U -. include .-> I4(("Decide trust (DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand)"))
1727:    E1(("Grade fails: stays Grading, failures shown")) -. extend .-> U
1728:    E2(("Unconfigured grader: 403")) -. extend .-> U
1729:    E3(("Rejected by operator (RejectAgentResponseCommand)")) -. extend .-> U
1730:```
1731:
1732:### 7.13 Use case: Retrieve trusted prior context [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-007]
1733:
1734:Actors: server (inside package construction), client apps. Basic flow: retrieval returns ranked candidates, only trusted responses among prior responses, preferring GraphRAG. Alternate flow: GraphRAG disabled, uninitialized, not indexed, or failing, and the deterministic relational path answers with the fallback reason.
1735:
1736:```mermaid
1737:flowchart LR
1738:    SV(["Server: package builder"]) --- U(("Retrieve trusted prior context (RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery)"))
1739:    CA(["Client apps"]) --- U
1740:    E1(("GraphRAG unavailable: relational fallback with reason")) -. extend .-> U
1741:```
1742:
1743:### 7.14 Use case: Maintain relationships, staleness, and supersession [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-005, -006]
1744:
1745:Actors: model, operator, server. Basic flow: links are created between packages, responses, requirements, turns, TODOs, code, and receipts; when a dependency changes, its dependents become stale; a newer response supersedes an older one. Alternate flows: invalid link, cycle, or unresolvable ref refused.
1746:
1747:```mermaid
1748:flowchart LR
1749:    MD(["Model"]) --- U(("Maintain relationships and staleness"))
1750:    OP(["Operator"]) --- U
1751:    SV(["Server"]) --- U
1752:    U -. include .-> I1(("Create, delete, query links (CreateAgentContextRelationshipCommand to QueryAgentContextRelationshipsQuery)"))
1753:    U -. include .-> I2(("Evaluate staleness (EvaluateStalenessCommand)"))
1754:    E1(("Supersede a response (SupersedeAgentResponseCommand)")) -. extend .-> U
1755:    E2(("Invalid link or cycle refused")) -. extend .-> U
1756:```
1757:
1758:### 7.15 Use case: Run a stateless or pilot invocation [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-009]
1759:
1760:Actors: operator, agent host and plugin, model. Basic flow: in `Stateless` mode the plugin builds the package for a delivered request and the model answers from the package alone; in `Pilot` mode the package is built and recorded but the model answers statefully; the pilot report compares both before any default changes. Alternate flows: mode `Off` keeps today's behavior; a build failure (operator, 2026-10-11: "Fail the invocation") refuses the prompt with the error code and message shown to the operator, produces no answer, and closes the turn `canceled`; a host whose prompt hook cannot refuse a prompt treats `Pilot` and `Stateless` as `Off`, with the limitation in its feature-matrix row.
1761:
1762:```mermaid
1763:flowchart LR
1764:    OP(["Operator"]) --- U(("Run a stateless or pilot invocation (RunStatelessInvocation)"))
1765:    HO(["Agent host and plugin"]) --- U
1766:    MD(["Model"]) --- U
1767:    U -. include .-> I1(("Build a context package for a request"))
1768:    U -. include .-> I2(("Submit and grade an agent response"))
1769:    E1(("Mode Off: stateful")) -. extend .-> U
1770:    E2(("Build fails: prompt refused, turn canceled")) -. extend .-> U
1771:    E3(("Pilot report (GetAgentContextPilotReportQuery)")) -. extend .-> U
1772:```
1773:
1774:### 7.16 Use case: Project responses into GraphRAG [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-007]
1775:
1776:Actors: server (background pass), operator. Basic flow: trusted responses are ingested into GraphRAG and responses that stop being trusted are removed. Alternate flows: GraphRAG disabled and every projection skipped; an ingest or delete error is recorded and retried on the next pass.
1777:

1779:flowchart LR
1780:    SV(["Server background pass"]) --- U(("Project responses into GraphRAG (ProjectAgentResponsesCommand)"))
1781:    OP(["Operator"]) --- U
1782:    E1(("GraphRAG disabled: skipped")) -. extend .-> U
1783:    E2(("Ingest or delete error: Failed, retried")) -. extend .-> U
1784:```

1698:### 7.11 Use case: Build a context package for a request [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001, -002]
1699:
1700:Actors: agent host and plugin, server. Precondition: the request's turn exists (UC-1) and the mode is `Pilot` or `Stateless`. Basic flow: the plugin asks the server to build a package for the request; the server gathers the request, profile, rules, applicable requirements, related turns, TODOs, receipts, trusted prior responses, and code at the current commit, filters secrets and untrusted items, ranks, fills the budget, records provenance, and returns the rendered package. Alternate flows: mandatory context exceeds the budget and the build fails with `agent_context_budget_exceeded`; the same idempotency key returns the same package; the commit is unreadable; replay proves the package is reproducible.

## Requirement ID Conventions

Three ID spaces are in use:

- **FR** - Functional Requirements: `^FR-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `FR-MCP-001`, `FR-AUTH-042`
- **TR** - Technical Requirements: `^TR-[A-Z]+-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TR-MCP-ARCH-001`, `TR-AUTH-SEC-002`
- **TEST** - Test Requirements: `^TEST-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TEST-MCP-001`, `TEST-AUTH-003`

All IDs must be uppercase. TR IDs require both an area and a subarea segment; FR and TEST IDs require only an area segment.

## Functional Requirements (FR)

### Listing FRs

To retrieve a filtered list of functional requirements:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.listFr
  params:
    area: MCP
    status: in_progress
```

All params are optional; omit to return all FRs. The result contains an `items` array:

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  result:
    items:
      - id: FR-MCP-001
        title: Agent authentication
        description: System must authenticate AI agents via API key
        status: completed
        priority: critical
        area: MCP
        createdAt: 2026-03-01T10:00:00Z
        updatedAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z
    totalCount: 1
```

Valid `status` values: `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `deferred`.

### Getting a Single FR

To fetch one functional requirement by ID:

```yaml
type: request
The special create-only value `ISSUE-NEW` instructs the server to create a GitHub issue, rewrite the stored ID to `ISSUE-{number}`, and return the canonical form. After the first sync, the `description` / `body` of an `ISSUE-{number}` TODO is immutable from the server side; subsequent update calls surface the change as a GitHub issue comment instead of overwriting the body.

When populating `dependsOn`, each dependency ID must also conform to these patterns.

## Querying TODOs

To retrieve a filtered list of TODOs:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-query-001
  method: workflow.todo.query
  params:
    keyword: authentication
    priority: high
    section: Backend
    done: false
```

All `params` fields are optional. Omit `params` entirely to return all TODOs. The response contains a paginated `items` array:

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-query-001
  result:
    items:
      - id: MCP-AUTH-001
        title: Implement JWT authentication
        section: Backend
        priority: high
        done: false
        estimate: 4h
        functionalRequirements: [FR-AUTH-001]
        technicalRequirements: [TR-AUTH-001]
    totalCount: 1
```

Valid `priority` values: `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`.

## Getting a Single TODO

To fetch the full detail of one TODO by ID:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-get-001
  method: workflow.todo.get
  params:
    id: MCP-AUTH-001
```

The result includes all fields: `implementationTasks`, `description`, `technicalDetails`, `remaining`, `doneSummary`, `dependsOn`, requirement arrays, and timestamps.

## Selecting a TODO as Active Context

To set a TODO as the active working context for the session:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-select-001
  method: workflow.todo.select
  params:
    id: MCP-AUTH-001
```

Once selected, `workflow.todo.updateSelected` may be used to patch fields without repeating the ID on every call.

## Requirement ID Conventions

Three ID spaces are in use:

- **FR** - Functional Requirements: `^FR-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `FR-MCP-001`, `FR-AUTH-042`
- **TR** - Technical Requirements: `^TR-[A-Z]+-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TR-MCP-ARCH-001`, `TR-AUTH-SEC-002`
- **TEST** - Test Requirements: `^TEST-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TEST-MCP-001`, `TEST-AUTH-003`

All IDs must be uppercase. TR IDs require both an area and a subarea segment; FR and TEST IDs require only an area segment.

## Functional Requirements (FR)

### Listing FRs

To retrieve a filtered list of functional requirements:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.listFr
  params:
    area: MCP
    status: in_progress
```

All params are optional; omit to return all FRs. The result contains an `items` array:

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  result:
    items:
      - id: FR-MCP-001
        title: Agent authentication
        description: System must authenticate AI agents via API key
        status: completed
        priority: critical
        area: MCP
        createdAt: 2026-03-01T10:00:00Z
        updatedAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z
    totalCount: 1
```

Valid `status` values: `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `deferred`.

### Getting a Single FR

To fetch one functional requirement by ID:

```yaml
type: request
The special create-only value `ISSUE-NEW` instructs the server to create a GitHub issue, rewrite the stored ID to `ISSUE-{number}`, and return the canonical form. After the first sync, the `description` / `body` of an `ISSUE-{number}` TODO is immutable from the server side; subsequent update calls surface the change as a GitHub issue comment instead of overwriting the body.

When populating `dependsOn`, each dependency ID must also conform to these patterns.

## Querying TODOs

To retrieve a filtered list of TODOs:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-query-001
  method: workflow.todo.query
  params:
    keyword: authentication
    priority: high
    section: Backend
    done: false
```

All `params` fields are optional. Omit `params` entirely to return all TODOs. The response contains a paginated `items` array:

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-query-001
  result:
    items:
      - id: MCP-AUTH-001
        title: Implement JWT authentication
        section: Backend
        priority: high
        done: false
        estimate: 4h
        functionalRequirements: [FR-AUTH-001]
        technicalRequirements: [TR-AUTH-001]
    totalCount: 1
```

Valid `priority` values: `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`.

## Getting a Single TODO

To fetch the full detail of one TODO by ID:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-get-001
  method: workflow.todo.get
  params:
    id: MCP-AUTH-001
```

The result includes all fields: `implementationTasks`, `description`, `technicalDetails`, `remaining`, `doneSummary`, `dependsOn`, requirement arrays, and timestamps.

## Selecting a TODO as Active Context

To set a TODO as the active working context for the session:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-select-001
  method: workflow.todo.select
  params:
    id: MCP-AUTH-001
```

Once selected, `workflow.todo.updateSelected` may be used to patch fields without repeating the ID on every call.

10:The operator requires an agent self-review and a hostile validation (HV) on every result, plus truthful, per-request audit in the MCP session log. Today:

28:
29:Turn logging
30:- Every user request (including messages queued mid-turn) is exactly one turn; actions and decisions map to the turn of the request that caused them, determined by the write-attribution rule below (D2). Enforcement of turn-logging correctness is Phase A and ships first.

34:- Request identity (operator D1, 2026-10-09: "have the server issue a request token when a message arrives"): the server mints every turn's `requestId` when a user message arrives (ingress), through the new mint operation `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint`. The mint call carries an idempotency nonce derived from the host's own identity for that message event (host binding table): a host per-prompt id, or a SHA-256 of host event fields that every delivery of that event carries identically. Every delivery of one event therefore sends the same nonce and receives the same token, including network retries and failsafe replay on every host and, on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id (codex `turn_id`, grok and grok-bot `promptId`, cline-v2 `runId`, opencode `messageID`) or the bridge's single ordered source (claude-code, claude-cowork), two hook processes started by a doubly registered hook (on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails closed); two separate user messages (including two intentionally identical prompts) are two events and receive two tokens. On copilot and classic cline, whose event fields include no per-message id, a message whose session, timestamp, and prompt all equal an already minted one is indistinguishable from a redelivery of it, so the host session fails closed under D6 instead of merging or guessing (host binding table, equal-field rule). The host id is only the idempotency key; the turn identity is the server-issued token. There is no prompt-text dedupe window. Every mint comes from a host arrival mechanism (a prompt hook, the arrival bridge, or a host-native hook adapter); no supported host relies on the model to mint. The stop gate's `duplicate_delivery_suspected` warning is a diagnostic only and is never counted as D1 compliance.
35:- Queued-message arrival (operator D5, 2026-10-09: "Arrival bridge"): a message the operator sends while a turn is running is minted when it is enqueued, not when the model later processes it. On hosts that record the enqueue in a transcript (Claude Code), a per-host-session arrival bridge started by the SessionStart hook tails the transcript and follows each queued message through the lifecycle the transcript records. Observed in this workspace's Claude Code transcripts on 2026-10-09: 117 `enqueue`, 79 `dequeue`, 35 `remove` (27 with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`), 2 `popAll`; a normal prompt is `enqueue` then `dequeue` within milliseconds, a mid-turn message is `enqueue` then `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn` when it is injected into the running turn (for example the operator's mid-turn message beginning "write a global memory with the" was removed with `absorbed_mid_turn` at 2026-10-09T14:35:47.730Z), and `popAll` pulls queued text back into the input box. The bridge mints at `enqueue` (state `queued`); the request becomes `delivered` at `dequeue` (applied by the bridge from the transcript itself; on hosts with a bridge the prompt hook neither mints nor claims) or at `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`; it becomes `withdrawn` at `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason. Task notifications and other system events that the host also enqueues are classified and never minted; on bridge hosts they keep their queue position (`kind: system`), so their `dequeue` never delivers a user request.

29:Turn logging
30:- Every user request (including messages queued mid-turn) is exactly one turn; actions and decisions map to the turn of the request that caused them, determined by the write-attribution rule below (D2). Enforcement of turn-logging correctness is Phase A and ships first.
31:- Plugin turn edits are independent: opening, editing, closing, or canceling one turn never changes another turn's local or server state; concurrent edits to different turns do not interfere.
32:- Unsupported-session failsafe (operator, 2026-10-10: "If QBrain is truly not available, use the failsafe already in the plugin." and, choosing between a failsafe capture and a warn-only Stop, "1"): when a host session fails closed under D6 (`unsupportedSince`), the model's session-log writes for a turn that was already open at that moment go to the plugin's existing failsafe instead of being refused (reviews excepted: they keep their no-failsafe rule and are recorded after the drain through the original pair), so the Stop gate's remedy stays accepted; the captured records drain at the next SessionStart through the trusted recovery flow with the turn's original pair (C5); every mint and every write for any other turn stays refused (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001).
33:- Clear-session closing rule (operator, 2026-10-10, choosing option A over leaving blocked and withdrawn turns open: "A"): clear-session completes each turn that meets the completion policy, fails each withdrawn turn (reason "withdrawn before delivery") and each turn the model marks blocked (with its blocker reason; `failed` requires `requestClass` only, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC002), and leaves every other turn in progress, reported by requestId with its exact missing items, never fabricating reviews (TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001). Definition (catalog cross-reference, not a change to the decision): "marked blocked" means the turn's `blockers` section (the existing decision-list field, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006-AC001) holds at least one nonblank model-authored entry, read by the clear-session coordinator for that turn by its original (`sessionId`, `requestId`) pair, and the first entry is the fail reason; precedence per turn: withdrawn -> `failTurn` ("withdrawn before delivery"); else blocked -> `failTurn` with the blocker reason (blocked takes precedence over a ready completion); else meets the completion policy -> `completeTurn`; else stays in progress, reported with its exact missing items. Close prerequisites (catalog cross-reference, not a change to the decision): before clear-session fails a withdrawn or blocked turn, the model writes by that turn's original pair, within the same clear-session run and before its session-end step, every prerequisite the plugin and the server require for that close, in the Stop gate remedy order (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009): a designDecision when the turn has no model evidence (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002), then a `requestClass` when it is missing or `Unclassified`, judged from the turn's `queryText`; the coordinator then fails the turn with its reason (TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001).
34:- Request identity (operator D1, 2026-10-09: "have the server issue a request token when a message arrives"): the server mints every turn's `requestId` when a user message arrives (ingress), through the new mint operation `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint`. The mint call carries an idempotency nonce derived from the host's own identity for that message event (host binding table): a host per-prompt id, or a SHA-256 of host event fields that every delivery of that event carries identically. Every delivery of one event therefore sends the same nonce and receives the same token, including network retries and failsafe replay on every host and, on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id (codex `turn_id`, grok and grok-bot `promptId`, cline-v2 `runId`, opencode `messageID`) or the bridge's single ordered source (claude-code, claude-cowork), two hook processes started by a doubly registered hook (on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails closed); two separate user messages (including two intentionally identical prompts) are two events and receive two tokens. On copilot and classic cline, whose event fields include no per-message id, a message whose session, timestamp, and prompt all equal an already minted one is indistinguishable from a redelivery of it, so the host session fails closed under D6 instead of merging or guessing (host binding table, equal-field rule). The host id is only the idempotency key; the turn identity is the server-issued token. There is no prompt-text dedupe window. Every mint comes from a host arrival mechanism (a prompt hook, the arrival bridge, or a host-native hook adapter); no supported host relies on the model to mint. The stop gate's `duplicate_delivery_suspected` warning is a diagnostic only and is never counted as D1 compliance.
35:- Queued-message arrival (operator D5, 2026-10-09: "Arrival bridge"): a message the operator sends while a turn is running is minted when it is enqueued, not when the model later processes it. On hosts that record the enqueue in a transcript (Claude Code), a per-host-session arrival bridge started by the SessionStart hook tails the transcript and follows each queued message through the lifecycle the transcript records. Observed in this workspace's Claude Code transcripts on 2026-10-09: 117 `enqueue`, 79 `dequeue`, 35 `remove` (27 with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`), 2 `popAll`; a normal prompt is `enqueue` then `dequeue` within milliseconds, a mid-turn message is `enqueue` then `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn` when it is injected into the running turn (for example the operator's mid-turn message beginning "write a global memory with the" was removed with `absorbed_mid_turn` at 2026-10-09T14:35:47.730Z), and `popAll` pulls queued text back into the input box. The bridge mints at `enqueue` (state `queued`); the request becomes `delivered` at `dequeue` (applied by the bridge from the transcript itself; on hosts with a bridge the prompt hook neither mints nor claims) or at `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`; it becomes `withdrawn` at `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason. Task notifications and other system events that the host also enqueues are classified and never minted; on bridge hosts they keep their queue position (`kind: system`), so their `dequeue` never delivers a user request.

39:- Write attribution (operator D2, 2026-10-09: tie each write to its request automatically through the agent app's hooks): every verb invocation is bound to one request automatically from host context, without the model naming it: the binding is the write target of the invoking host session at the moment the invocation starts, captured once and stored immutably with that invocation (its persist record and failsafe record), so a later message never retargets an invocation already started. A host session's write target is the request most recently delivered to the model in that host session: a prompt the host hands to the model as a new turn (the prompt hook on hosts without a bridge, or the bridge's `dequeue` delivery), or a queued message absorbed into the running turn (`absorbed_mid_turn`). Minting alone never moves the write target, so work the model is still doing for request R1 after R2 is enqueued stays on R1 until R2 is delivered. Explicit `requestId` remains accepted as an override, for example to continue R1 work after R2 was absorbed, and it is required while two or more delivered requests are open in the host session (D9). Attribution therefore maps each write to the request most recently delivered to the model in its host session when the write started. A write is never attributed by guesswork: when a verb cannot read its host session key from its own invocation context (host binding table), it binds only if exactly one live host session of its agent exists in the workspace (warning `host_session_inferred`); with none it is refused (`host_session_unknown`), and with more than one it is refused (`host_session_ambiguous`), in both cases unless it carries the trusted recovery or review-backfill pair (original MCP `sessionId` and `requestId`, verified against the server for this workspace and agent, C5); an explicit `requestId` alone never lets a verb without a host session key write. No verb ever targets the workspace-level `current-turn.yaml`.
40:- Ambiguous attribution (operator D9, 2026-10-09: "Refuse when ambiguous"): no host supplies a per-action signal of which request caused a write, so automatic binding applies only while exactly one delivered request is open in the host session. While two or more delivered requests are open (for example R2 absorbed mid-turn while R1 is still open), a write without an explicit `requestId` is refused with `request_ambiguous`, naming the open requests; the model passes `requestId` until all but one are closed. Writes are never attributed by guesswork.

48:- Fields: `status` (`Unnecessary` | `Unstarted` | `Running` | `Pass` | `Fail` | `Other`), `otherNotes`, `correctness`, `completeness` (lossless decimal 0..1), `correctnessThreshold`, `completenessThreshold` (server-stamped, read-only), `reasons` (string[]), `reviewer`, `reviewedAt` (UTC), `requestJsonlPath`, `responseJsonlPath`. No `passed` bool.
49:- One record per kind per turn; latest write wins.
50:- Server creates both at turn creation as `Unstarted`. `hostileReview` flips to `Unnecessary` when `requestClass` becomes `Chore`, and back to `Unstarted` if the class changes away while still `Unnecessary`. Records past `Unstarted`/`Unnecessary` are never auto-changed. Legacy turns are backfilled `agentReview=Unstarted`, `hostileReview=Unstarted`. (Catalog cross-references, not a change to the decision: the flip and its reverse apply only to in-progress turns, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-006-AC002 and UC-4; a reset restores the creation default for the turn's current class, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001-AC004.)
51:- `otherNotes` with text is rejected unless `status` is `Other`.
52:- Strict per-status fields: `Unnecessary`/`Unstarted` carry no scores, reasons, reviewer, timestamps, or paths; `Running` requires `reviewer`, forbids scores; `Pass`/`Fail` require `correctness`, `completeness`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`; `hostileReview` `Pass`/`Fail` also require `requestJsonlPath` and `responseJsonlPath`; `Other` requires non-empty `otherNotes` (the Other reason; operator D4, 2026-10-09: "Other requires Other Reason be populated") and allows optional scores, `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`, and receipt paths. `Unnecessary` is server-managed only.
53:- Thresholds: `Mcp:SessionLog:ReviewThresholds:{Agent|Hostile}:{Correctness|Completeness}` (decimal 0..1, per instance through `McpInstanceResolver` overrides), default 0.98, inclusive (score >= threshold passes). Pass requires both scores to meet their thresholds. The server derives `Pass`/`Fail`; a supplied `Pass`/`Fail` that contradicts the derivation is rejected (422 `review_status_conflict`); omitting status lets the server derive it. `Other` is never derived. Thresholds in force are stamped on the record.
54:- Names stay `correctness`/`completeness`. HV tooling maps `accuracy` -> `correctness` and integer percent -> decimal/100.

29:Turn logging
30:- Every user request (including messages queued mid-turn) is exactly one turn; actions and decisions map to the turn of the request that caused them, determined by the write-attribution rule below (D2). Enforcement of turn-logging correctness is Phase A and ships first.
31:- Plugin turn edits are independent: opening, editing, closing, or canceling one turn never changes another turn's local or server state; concurrent edits to different turns do not interfere.
32:- Unsupported-session failsafe (operator, 2026-10-10: "If QBrain is truly not available, use the failsafe already in the plugin." and, choosing between a failsafe capture and a warn-only Stop, "1"): when a host session fails closed under D6 (`unsupportedSince`), the model's session-log writes for a turn that was already open at that moment go to the plugin's existing failsafe instead of being refused (reviews excepted: they keep their no-failsafe rule and are recorded after the drain through the original pair), so the Stop gate's remedy stays accepted; the captured records drain at the next SessionStart through the trusted recovery flow with the turn's original pair (C5); every mint and every write for any other turn stays refused (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001).
33:- Clear-session closing rule (operator, 2026-10-10, choosing option A over leaving blocked and withdrawn turns open: "A"): clear-session completes each turn that meets the completion policy, fails each withdrawn turn (reason "withdrawn before delivery") and each turn the model marks blocked (with its blocker reason; `failed` requires `requestClass` only, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC002), and leaves every other turn in progress, reported by requestId with its exact missing items, never fabricating reviews (TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001). Definition (catalog cross-reference, not a change to the decision): "marked blocked" means the turn's `blockers` section (the existing decision-list field, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006-AC001) holds at least one nonblank model-authored entry, read by the clear-session coordinator for that turn by its original (`sessionId`, `requestId`) pair, and the first entry is the fail reason; precedence per turn: withdrawn -> `failTurn` ("withdrawn before delivery"); else blocked -> `failTurn` with the blocker reason (blocked takes precedence over a ready completion); else meets the completion policy -> `completeTurn`; else stays in progress, reported with its exact missing items. Close prerequisites (catalog cross-reference, not a change to the decision): before clear-session fails a withdrawn or blocked turn, the model writes by that turn's original pair, within the same clear-session run and before its session-end step, every prerequisite the plugin and the server require for that close, in the Stop gate remedy order (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009): a designDecision when the turn has no model evidence (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002), then a `requestClass` when it is missing or `Unclassified`, judged from the turn's `queryText`; the coordinator then fails the turn with its reason (TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001).
34:- Request identity (operator D1, 2026-10-09: "have the server issue a request token when a message arrives"): the server mints every turn's `requestId` when a user message arrives (ingress), through the new mint operation `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint`. The mint call carries an idempotency nonce derived from the host's own identity for that message event (host binding table): a host per-prompt id, or a SHA-256 of host event fields that every delivery of that event carries identically. Every delivery of one event therefore sends the same nonce and receives the same token, including network retries and failsafe replay on every host and, on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id (codex `turn_id`, grok and grok-bot `promptId`, cline-v2 `runId`, opencode `messageID`) or the bridge's single ordered source (claude-code, claude-cowork), two hook processes started by a doubly registered hook (on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails closed); two separate user messages (including two intentionally identical prompts) are two events and receive two tokens. On copilot and classic cline, whose event fields include no per-message id, a message whose session, timestamp, and prompt all equal an already minted one is indistinguishable from a redelivery of it, so the host session fails closed under D6 instead of merging or guessing (host binding table, equal-field rule). The host id is only the idempotency key; the turn identity is the server-issued token. There is no prompt-text dedupe window. Every mint comes from a host arrival mechanism (a prompt hook, the arrival bridge, or a host-native hook adapter); no supported host relies on the model to mint. The stop gate's `duplicate_delivery_suspected` warning is a diagnostic only and is never counted as D1 compliance.
35:- Queued-message arrival (operator D5, 2026-10-09: "Arrival bridge"): a message the operator sends while a turn is running is minted when it is enqueued, not when the model later processes it. On hosts that record the enqueue in a transcript (Claude Code), a per-host-session arrival bridge started by the SessionStart hook tails the transcript and follows each queued message through the lifecycle the transcript records. Observed in this workspace's Claude Code transcripts on 2026-10-09: 117 `enqueue`, 79 `dequeue`, 35 `remove` (27 with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`), 2 `popAll`; a normal prompt is `enqueue` then `dequeue` within milliseconds, a mid-turn message is `enqueue` then `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn` when it is injected into the running turn (for example the operator's mid-turn message beginning "write a global memory with the" was removed with `absorbed_mid_turn` at 2026-10-09T14:35:47.730Z), and `popAll` pulls queued text back into the input box. The bridge mints at `enqueue` (state `queued`); the request becomes `delivered` at `dequeue` (applied by the bridge from the transcript itself; on hosts with a bridge the prompt hook neither mints nor claims) or at `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`; it becomes `withdrawn` at `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason. Task notifications and other system events that the host also enqueues are classified and never minted; on bridge hosts they keep their queue position (`kind: system`), so their `dequeue` never delivers a user request.
36:- Hosts without an arrival mechanism (operator D6, 2026-10-09: "Adapters or unsupported"): a host is supported for turn logging only through an arrival mechanism this plan specifies (a prompt hook that fires at enqueue, the claude-code/claude-cowork arrival bridge, or the classic-cline native-hook adapter); every other host is unsupported until a separately approved adapter exists, and a queue or enqueue event that P0.2 records on such a host becomes a traced follow-up adapter TODO (filed in P0.8) for operator approval (host binding table). The limitations live in `docs/AGENT-PLUGIN-FEATURE-MATRIX.md` (one row per plugin and feature: supported, adapted, or limited, with the reason and the receipt), first written in P0.8 from the P0.2 receipts, updated in A9 and S11, and checked by a docs contract test.

39:- Write attribution (operator D2, 2026-10-09: tie each write to its request automatically through the agent app's hooks): every verb invocation is bound to one request automatically from host context, without the model naming it: the binding is the write target of the invoking host session at the moment the invocation starts, captured once and stored immutably with that invocation (its persist record and failsafe record), so a later message never retargets an invocation already started. A host session's write target is the request most recently delivered to the model in that host session: a prompt the host hands to the model as a new turn (the prompt hook on hosts without a bridge, or the bridge's `dequeue` delivery), or a queued message absorbed into the running turn (`absorbed_mid_turn`). Minting alone never moves the write target, so work the model is still doing for request R1 after R2 is enqueued stays on R1 until R2 is delivered. Explicit `requestId` remains accepted as an override, for example to continue R1 work after R2 was absorbed, and it is required while two or more delivered requests are open in the host session (D9). Attribution therefore maps each write to the request most recently delivered to the model in its host session when the write started. A write is never attributed by guesswork: when a verb cannot read its host session key from its own invocation context (host binding table), it binds only if exactly one live host session of its agent exists in the workspace (warning `host_session_inferred`); with none it is refused (`host_session_unknown`), and with more than one it is refused (`host_session_ambiguous`), in both cases unless it carries the trusted recovery or review-backfill pair (original MCP `sessionId` and `requestId`, verified against the server for this workspace and agent, C5); an explicit `requestId` alone never lets a verb without a host session key write. No verb ever targets the workspace-level `current-turn.yaml`.
40:- Ambiguous attribution (operator D9, 2026-10-09: "Refuse when ambiguous"): no host supplies a per-action signal of which request caused a write, so automatic binding applies only while exactly one delivered request is open in the host session. While two or more delivered requests are open (for example R2 absorbed mid-turn while R1 is still open), a write without an explicit `requestId` is refused with `request_ambiguous`, naming the open requests; the model passes `requestId` until all but one are closed. Writes are never attributed by guesswork.
41:- Copilot duplicate deliveries (operator D11, 2026-10-09: "Supported only if single hook"): Copilot gives no stable per-prompt id and separately registered hooks may see different `timestamp` values, so Copilot turn logging is supported only while the plugin's duplicate check proves exactly one MCP prompt hook across all Copilot hook sources; otherwise the Copilot prompt hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` before any mint, and the condition is a D7 documented limitation until fixed. One Copilot prompt therefore never becomes two turns.
42:- Node runtime floor (operator D12, 2026-10-09: "Keep Node 18/20"), superseded for core code by the 2026-10-11 PowerShell-only ruling: no code of this plan runs on Node except the logic-free TypeScript-host adapters, which keep each host's declared engine unchanged (mcpserver-cline-plugin, mcpserver-cline-v2-plugin, and mcpserver-opencode-plugin `>=18`; the Cline application's own `node >=22` is unaffected). Exact review scores are validated and carried by the PowerShell core's raw-lexeme rules (S8); the adapters never parse a score (C10).

44:Request class
45:- Turn scalar `requestClass`: `Code` | `Docs` | `Chore` (case-insensitive in, canonical PascalCase out, anything else rejected). Required, enforced at transition to `completed` or `failed`, not at creation (hooks create turns before the agent can classify). Legacy rows backfilled to `Unclassified` (readable; never accepted on new writes from agent surfaces).
46:
47:Review record (shared by `agentReview` and `hostileReview`)
48:- Fields: `status` (`Unnecessary` | `Unstarted` | `Running` | `Pass` | `Fail` | `Other`), `otherNotes`, `correctness`, `completeness` (lossless decimal 0..1), `correctnessThreshold`, `completenessThreshold` (server-stamped, read-only), `reasons` (string[]), `reviewer`, `reviewedAt` (UTC), `requestJsonlPath`, `responseJsonlPath`. No `passed` bool.
49:- One record per kind per turn; latest write wins.
50:- Server creates both at turn creation as `Unstarted`. `hostileReview` flips to `Unnecessary` when `requestClass` becomes `Chore`, and back to `Unstarted` if the class changes away while still `Unnecessary`. Records past `Unstarted`/`Unnecessary` are never auto-changed. Legacy turns are backfilled `agentReview=Unstarted`, `hostileReview=Unstarted`. (Catalog cross-references, not a change to the decision: the flip and its reverse apply only to in-progress turns, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-006-AC002 and UC-4; a reset restores the creation default for the turn's current class, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001-AC004.)
51:- `otherNotes` with text is rejected unless `status` is `Other`.
52:- Strict per-status fields: `Unnecessary`/`Unstarted` carry no scores, reasons, reviewer, timestamps, or paths; `Running` requires `reviewer`, forbids scores; `Pass`/`Fail` require `correctness`, `completeness`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`; `hostileReview` `Pass`/`Fail` also require `requestJsonlPath` and `responseJsonlPath`; `Other` requires non-empty `otherNotes` (the Other reason; operator D4, 2026-10-09: "Other requires Other Reason be populated") and allows optional scores, `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`, and receipt paths. `Unnecessary` is server-managed only.
53:- Thresholds: `Mcp:SessionLog:ReviewThresholds:{Agent|Hostile}:{Correctness|Completeness}` (decimal 0..1, per instance through `McpInstanceResolver` overrides), default 0.98, inclusive (score >= threshold passes). Pass requires both scores to meet their thresholds. The server derives `Pass`/`Fail`; a supplied `Pass`/`Fail` that contradicts the derivation is rejected (422 `review_status_conflict`); omitting status lets the server derive it. `Other` is never derived. Thresholds in force are stamped on the record.
54:- Names stay `correctness`/`completeness`. HV tooling maps `accuracy` -> `correctness` and integer percent -> decimal/100.
55:
56:Completion rules
57:- `completed` requires `requestClass` plus `agentReview.status` in `Pass`/`Fail`/`Other`; for `Code`/`Docs` also `hostileReview.status` in `Pass`/`Fail`/`Other`; for `Chore` `hostileReview` is not checked (HV not required). `Unstarted`/`Running` block where checked. Pass is not required (Fail/Other complete).
58:- `failed` requires `requestClass` only. Reviews remain writable on terminal turns.
59:- Server-internal writers (QuadBrain chat, AuditedAgentCliClient, WorkspacePolicyService, federation replication, transcript/session ingestion) are exempt by code-path origin; they never fabricate reviews.

61:Scope and process

## Summary
Create `docs/Stateless-Agent-Context-Management.md` as the decision-complete BDPv4 plan for stateless agent requests.

- Store packages, responses, grades, and relationships in the relational store as authoritative records.

# Agent Instructions

## Session Start

1. Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` in the repo root for the current API key and endpoints.
2. For specific operational steps (session bootstrap, session log turn workflow, and helper command sequence), follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.

On every subsequent user message:

1. Follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` for specific operational instructions.
2. Complete the user's request.

## Rules

1. `templates/prompt-templates.yaml` (`default-marker-prompt`) is the source of truth for specific agent instructions. `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` is the rendered runtime instruction set.
2. Keep this file focused on durable workspace policy and conventions; avoid duplicating marker-file operational procedures.
3. Use helper modules for session log and TODO operations. Do not make raw API calls.
4. Persist session log updates immediately after each meaningful change (turn creation, action append, decision, requirement, blocker, file/context update). Do not defer saves.
5. Capture rich turn detail: interpretation, response, status, actions (type/status/filePath), contextList, filesModified, designDecisions, requirementsDiscovered, blockers, and relevant processing dialog.
6. Follow workspace conventions in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` for build, test, and architecture guidance.
7. Use **only `pwsh.exe`** for shell commands and script execution; do not use `powershell.exe`.
8. When you need API schemas, module examples, or compliance rules, load them from `docs/context/` or use `context_search`.
9. Do not fabricate information. If you made a mistake, acknowledge it. Distinguish facts from speculation.
10. Prioritize correctness over speed. Do not ship code you have not verified compiles and is logically sound.
11. When writing session logs or other audit records, agents must identify themselves accurately using their real agent identity in Pascal-Case. Do not use placeholder, legacy, or misleading sourceType values.
12. Never edit YAML by appending, replacing, or removing text lines. Deserialize the complete document into an object, mutate the object, serialize it, and save it. Use `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` for PowerShell work.

## Byrd Test Gate

The canonical process is `docs/Development-Process-draft-v4.md`. To leave a Byrd implementation slice, the entire unit test suite for the current iteration and previous iterations must be completely passing. In this workspace, skipped tests are not passing tests: a validation gate requires zero failures and zero skips in the executed scope. Tests should directly track progress; deferred work belongs in MCP TODO/requirements state until that slice starts, not in skipped test placeholders.

## Where Things Live

- `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` — connection details, API key, workspace config (regenerated on server start)
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — build/test commands, architecture overview, coding conventions
- `docs/context/` — on-demand reference docs (schemas, module docs, compliance rules, action types)
- `docs/Project/` — requirements docs, TODO.yaml, mapping matrices
- `templates/` — prompt templates (loaded on demand)
- `tools/powershell/McpContext.psm1` — PowerShell module for context ingestion/query workflows
- `tools/powershell/McpContext.USER.md` — user-level guide for the McpContext module
- `tools/powershell/McpContext.AGENT.md` — agent workflow instructions for the McpContext module
- `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` — object-first YAML mutation helper for agents and plugin maintenance

## MCP Interaction via REPL Tools

Agents running inside `McpAgent` must use the 27 built-in tools instead of raw HTTP calls. See `docs/REPL-MIGRATION-GUIDE.md` for the full tool inventory and migration patterns.

Key rules:
- Use `mcp_session_*` tools for session log lifecycle (bootstrap, turns, history).
- Use `mcp_todo_*` tools for TODO CRUD (query, get, create, update, delete, plan, status, implementation).
- Use `mcp_requirements_*` tools for FR/TR/TEST queries.
- Use `mcp_client_invoke` for any sub-client method not covered by a dedicated tool (context search, GitHub, workspace, etc.).
- Do not make raw HTTP calls to `/qbrainai/*` endpoints when a tool is available.

## Context Loading by Task Type

- Agent Help: see marker `## Agent Help (QBrain.AI issues)` in `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`; API `/qbrainai/agent-help`
- Session logging → `docs/context/session-log-schema.md` + `docs/context/module-bootstrap.md`
- TODO management → `docs/context/todo-schema.md` + `docs/context/module-bootstrap.md`
- API integration → `docs/context/api-capabilities.md` (or `GET /swagger/v1/swagger.json`)
- Adding dependencies → `docs/context/compliance-rules.md`
- Logging actions → `docs/context/action-types.md`
- New to workspace → this file + `docs/context/api-capabilities.md`
- Migrating from raw API → `docs/REPL-MIGRATION-GUIDE.md`

## Agent Conduct

You represent the workspace owner. Your work directly reflects the owner's professional reputation.

### Honesty

- Do not fabricate information, capabilities, or results.
- Distinguish between facts, informed opinions, and speculation.
- Acknowledge mistakes immediately and correct them.

### Correctness

- Prioritize correctness over speed.
- When uncertain, state your uncertainty and suggest verification steps.
- Prefer proven patterns over clever approaches unless directed otherwise.
- All code must have XMLDocs. All public APIs must be documented.
- Follow DRY, SOLID, and existing project conventions.

### Decision Documentation

- Log every decision to the session log, including trivial ones.
- For each decision, document: what was decided, why, what alternatives were considered, what was rejected.
- Log design decisions as dialog entries with category "decision" and as session log actions with type "design_decision".

### Professional Representation

- Every interaction is audited via the session log.
- Every commit must be correct, clean, well-described, and complete.
- Log all commits as actions with type "commit" (SHA, branch, message, files).
- Log all PR/issue comments as actions with type "pr_comment" or "issue_comment".
- Always sign PR comments using the same signature convention as commits, identifying the actual authoring agent.

### Source Attribution

- Document all web sources in the session log as actions with type "web_reference" (URL, title, usage).
- Add source URLs to the turn's contextList array.
- Attribute external code in both the session log and code comments.

## Requirements Tracking

When you discover or agree on new requirements during a session:

1. Update the files in `docs/Project/`:
   - `Functional-Requirements.md` — append FR-MCP-* entries
   - `Technical-Requirements.md` — append TR-MCP-* entries
   - `TR-per-FR-Mapping.md` — append mapping rows
   - `Requirements-Matrix.md` — append status rows
   - `Testing-Requirements.md` — append TEST-MCP-* entries
2. Include the requirement ID in your session log turn's tags.
3. Capture requirements as they emerge. Do not defer to later.

## Design Decision Logging

When a design decision is made:

1. Log it as a session log dialog item with category "decision".
2. Include: the decision, alternatives considered, rationale, and affected requirements.
3. Add a session log action with type "design_decision".
4. If the decision affects existing code or requirements, note what needs updating.

## Session Continuity

At the start of every session:

1. Follow the session-start checklist in `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
2. Read `docs/Project/Requirements-Matrix.md` to understand project state.
3. If resuming interrupted work, review the last session's pending decisions.

At regular intervals during long sessions (~10 interactions):

1. Follow marker-file update cadence and session logging requirements from `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
2. Ensure all design decisions are captured.
3. Verify requirements docs are up to date.

## Glossary

- **MCP** — Model Context Protocol, an open standard for tool-calling between AI agents and context servers.
- **Workspace** — a project directory registered with the MCP server. All workspaces share a single port; use the `X-Workspace-Path` header to target a specific one.
- **Marker File** — the `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` file at each workspace root. Contains connection details, auth token, and agent prompt.
- **API Key** — a per-workspace cryptographic token that rotates on each server restart. Required for all `/qbrainai/*` REST endpoints.
- **Streamable HTTP** — the MCP wire protocol transport at `/mcp-transport`. Carries JSON-RPC tool calls over HTTP POST with streaming responses.
- **Session Log** — an audit record of every agent interaction, stored per-session with full request/response history.
- **Context Pack** — an ordered set of document chunks retrieved by semantic + full-text hybrid search, scoped to the workspace.
- **Tool Bucket** — a GitHub repository containing tool manifest files, similar to a Scoop package bucket.

## Response Formatting

- Do not use table-style output in responses.
- Use concise bullets or short paragraphs instead.

#Requires -Version 7.0
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Runs an analyzer-checked PowerShell review command and records sanitized evidence.
.DESCRIPTION
The caller supplies only review reads, receipt writes, and the reviewer's own
session-log operations. The MCP cache is isolated outside the worktree.
.PARAMETER CommandText
PowerShell source to analyze before executing.
#>
[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$CommandText)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module PSScriptAnalyzer -RequiredVersion 1.25.0
$parseTokens = $null
$parseErrors = $null
$null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseInput($CommandText, [ref]$parseTokens, [ref]$parseErrors)
if ($parseErrors.Count -gt 0) { throw ($parseErrors | Out-String) }
$diagnostics = @(Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -ScriptDefinition $CommandText -Severity Warning,Error)
if ($diagnostics.Count -gt 0) { throw ($diagnostics | Format-List | Out-String) }
if (-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess('Review evidence and reviewer session only', $CommandText)) { return }

$reviewRoot = '/home/sharpninja/github/McpServer/.claude/worktrees/session-20261009'
$env:MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH = '/home/sharpninja/github/McpServer'
$env:CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT = '/home/sharpninja/.codex/plugins/cache/mcpserver-codex-plugin/mcpserver/1.119.0'
$env:MCP_CACHE_DIR_OVERRIDE = '/tmp/hv-plan-readiness-r4-20261012T034439Z-cache'
$null = New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $env:MCP_CACHE_DIR_OVERRIDE -Force
$env:MCPSERVER_FAILSAFE_DIR = Join-Path $env:MCP_CACHE_DIR_OVERRIDE 'failsafe'
$env:MCP_FAILSAFE_DRAIN_DISABLED = '1'
$env:MCP_SESSION_MODEL = 'gpt-6-astra'
Set-Location -LiteralPath $reviewRoot
$started = [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('o')
$global:LASTEXITCODE = 0
$commandExit = 0
try {
    $result = & ([scriptblock]::Create($CommandText)) 2>&1 | Out-String -Width 240
    $commandExit = $global:LASTEXITCODE
} catch {
    $result = $_ | Out-String

}

$keyMatch = [regex]::Match($marker, '(?m)^apiKey:\s*(\S+)')
if ($keyMatch.Success) { $result = $result.Replace($keyMatch.Groups[1].Value, '[REDACTED:api-key]') }
$result = [regex]::Replace($result, '(?i)((?:apiKey|api_key|X-Api-Key)["'']?\s*[:=]\s*["'']?)[A-Za-z0-9_+/=.-]{20,}', '$1[REDACTED:api-key]')

Write-Output $result
Write-Output ('COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=' + $commandExit)
