107: Host binding table (locks the D1 nonce source, the D5 arrival source, and the D2 host session key per host; every turn token is still minted by the server). Rules common to all hosts:
108: - Nonce: computed from the event itself, never from the hook process, so every delivery of one event yields the same nonce; a value outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$` is replaced by the 64 lowercase hex characters of its SHA-256. Equal-field rule (copilot and classic cline, whose nonce hashes event fields with no per-message id): under `turn-open.lock`, a new prompt-hook invocation whose nonce already has a failsafe mint record or a `pending-<nonce>` turn in that host session, or whose mint returns `merged`, cannot be told apart from a separate message with equal session, timestamp, and prompt, so it mints and binds nothing and the host session fails closed under D6 exactly as the bridge does for an unattributable record (`unsupportedSince: { causeNonce, causeOperation: prompt_hook, reason: indistinguishable_arrival }` with the session-level envelope; every session-log verb then reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until the session ends, except that writes for a turn already open at that moment go to the plugin failsafe under the unsupported-session failsafe rule, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001; its open turns are listed at the next SessionStart). A network retry or failsafe replay of a stored mint record is a drain of that record, not a new invocation, and reuses its nonce without failing closed.
109: - Unsupported-session rule (D6; operator option 1 of 2026-10-10): every check that makes a host session report `turn_logging_unsupported` after one of its requests was delivered records `unsupportedSince` with the session-level envelope in `turn-state.yaml` in the same atomic replace that makes the session unsupported, with `reason` set to that check's code: `queue_removal_ambiguous` (bridge), `indistinguishable_arrival` (equal-field rule), `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` (an unknown queue operation, a record missing a required field, or a transcript shorter than `appliedThroughOffset`), `duplicate_prompt_hook` (the copilot or classic-cline single-registration check starts failing; the first verb or hook in that host session that observes it records it), or, for any other D6 check, its own reason code; plus `causeOffset` or `causeNonce` where the cause has one, else `detectedAtUtc`. Whatever the reason, the unsupported-session failsafe of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 then applies: writes for a turn of that host session still in progress when `unsupportedSince` was recorded (a delivered open request, or a `withdrawn` queue entry still `in_progress`, addressed by its original pair; a minted request still `queued` is not covered and stays a warning) are captured, and every mint and every other write is refused. A network retry or failsafe replay of a stored mint record is a drain of that record, not a new invocation, and reuses its nonce without failing closed.
109: - Unsupported-session rule (D6; operator option 1 of 2026-10-10): every check that makes a host session report `turn_logging_unsupported` after one of its requests was delivered records `unsupportedSince` with the session-level envelope in `turn-state.yaml` in the same atomic replace that makes the session unsupported, with `reason` set to that check's code: `queue_removal_ambiguous` (bridge), `indistinguishable_arrival` (equal-field rule), `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` (an unknown queue operation, a record missing a required field, or a transcript shorter than `appliedThroughOffset`), `duplicate_prompt_hook` (the copilot or classic-cline single-registration check starts failing; the first verb or hook in that host session that observes it records it), or, for any other D6 check, its own reason code; plus `causeOffset` or `causeNonce` where the cause has one, else `detectedAtUtc`. The state lasts until the host session ends, or until a SessionStart clears its cause where the cause's own rule allows (the bridge restarting on a valid transcript); the captured records drain at that SessionStart. 107: Host binding table (locks the D1 nonce source, the D5 arrival source, and the D2 host session key per host; every turn token is still minted by the server). Rules common to all hosts:
108: - Nonce: computed from the event itself, never from the hook process, so every delivery of one event yields the same nonce; a value outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$` is replaced by the 64 lowercase hex characters of its SHA-256. Equal-field rule (copilot and classic cline, whose nonce hashes event fields with no per-message id): under `turn-open.lock`, a new prompt-hook invocation whose nonce already has a failsafe mint record or a `pending-<nonce>` turn in that host session, or whose mint returns `merged`, cannot be told apart from a separate message with equal session, timestamp, and prompt, so it mints and binds nothing and the host session fails closed under D6 exactly as the bridge does for an unattributable record (`unsupportedSince: { causeNonce, causeOperation: prompt_hook, reason: indistinguishable_arrival }` with the session-level envelope; every session-log verb then reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until the session ends, except that writes for a turn already open at that moment go to the plugin failsafe under the unsupported-session failsafe rule, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001; its open turns are listed at the next SessionStart). A network retry or failsafe replay of a stored mint record is a drain of that record, not a new invocation, and reuses its nonce without failing closed.
109: - Unsupported-session rule (D6; operator option 1 of 2026-10-10): every check that makes a host session report `turn_logging_unsupported` after one of its requests was delivered records `unsupportedSince` with the session-level envelope in `turn-state.yaml` in the same atomic replace that makes the session unsupported, with `reason` set to that check's code: `queue_removal_ambiguous` (bridge), `indistinguishable_arrival` (equal-field rule), `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` (an unknown queue operation, a record missing a required field, or a transcript shorter than `appliedThroughOffset`), `duplicate_prompt_hook` (the copilot or classic-cline single-registration check starts failing; the first verb or hook in that host session that observes it records it), or, for any other D6 check, its own reason code; plus `causeOffset` or `causeNonce` where the cause has one, else `detectedAtUtc`. Whatever the reason, the unsupported-session failsafe of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 then applies: writes for a turn of that host session still in progress when `unsupportedSince` was recorded (a delivered open request, or a `withdrawn` queue entry still `in_progress`, addressed by its original pair; a minted request still `queued` is not covered and stays a warning) are captured, and every mint and every other write is refused. The state lasts until the host session ends, or until a SessionStart clears its cause where the cause's own rule allows (the bridge restarting on a valid transcript); the captured records drain at that SessionStart. A host that is unsupported from its first event mints nothing, has no open turn, and records no `unsupportedSince`.
110: - P0.2 gating rule (D6, D7): every case, gate, or live assertion that needs a host's arrival mechanism or a P0.2-probed host field runs only when that host's P0.2 row passed; when the row failed or was unavailable, the host's D6 case `<Host>_P0_2NotPassed_TurnLoggingUnsupported_ZeroMintsZeroWrites` runs instead in the same slice (A3: `ClaudeCode_P0_2NotPassed_TurnLoggingUnsupported_ZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `Grok_P0_2NotPassed_TurnLoggingUnsupported_ZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `GrokBot_P0_2NotPassed_TurnLoggingUnsupported_ZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `Copilot_P0_2NotPassed_TurnLoggingUnsupported_ZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `Cowork_P0_2NotPassed_TurnLoggingUnsupported_ZeroMintsZeroWrites`; A8: `Cline_P0_2NotPassed_TurnLoggingUnsupported_ZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `ClineV2_P0_2NotPassed_TurnLoggingUnsupported_ZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `OpenCode_P0_2NotPassed_TurnLoggingUnsupported_ZeroMintsZeroWrites`), and every live check excludes that host with its P0.2 receipt (codex excepted: a failed or unavailable codex row, or a codex enqueue-versus-processing result of "only when processed", stops P0 instead, because every HV reviewer persists its own turn through the Codex plugin; host binding table, codex). The P0.2 outcome that selected each branch is that host's feature-matrix receipt. The Cowork bridge fixtures of A3, the per-host mint cases of A3 (codex, grok, grok-bot, copilot) and A8 (classic cline, cline-v2, opencode), the copilot duplicate-hook transition of A9, TEST-MCP-PLUGIN-013-AC001, the codex live assertion, and the Phase A live check on claude-code are instances of this rule.
111: - Host session key: read from the verb's own invocation context as listed per host. Long-lived processes (stdio MCP servers, the arrival bridge itself) never trust a key captured at spawn time, because a host may change the session in place (Claude Code `/clear`; resume without an explicit id keeps the startup id in long-lived subprocesses per the Claude Code env-var reference); they resolve the key per call by the live-session rule.
112: - Queued-message arrival on every host (D5, D6): P0.2 records, per host, whether a message sent while a turn is running reaches an arrival mechanism at enqueue. Where the prompt event itself fires at enqueue for a message the host takes into the running turn, it is the arrival mechanism; a prompt event that fires at enqueue for a message the host runs as its own later turn is not, because a prompt-hook mint is delivered at once (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-005) and would move the write target and the stop ledger to a request the model has not received (D2; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001), so P0.2 records that result as only when processed. A `queue-operation` with an unknown operation or a missing required field is never skipped: the bridge stops before it without advancing `appliedThroughOffset`, records warning `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` and, after a delivered request, `unsupportedSince` with that reason and the record's `causeOffset` in the same atomic replace (unsupported-session rule), and the host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb (D6) until a verified adapter handles that shape, while writes for a turn already open go to the plugin failsafe (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001). Records are applied by whichever process holds `turn-open.lock`: the bridge, or a session-log verb, which first records the transcript length at the moment the invocation starts and, after taking the lock, applies every pending record that ends at or before that length, never a record appended later, before it binds (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC006), so a verb started after a `dequeue` line was written binds to that request, and a `dequeue` appended after the verb started never retargets it (D2). The prompt hook on claude-code and claude-cowork neither mints nor claims; it classifies system events and starts no turn. P0.2 verifies that every user prompt (in each prompt form of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009) produces an `enqueue` record and that `dequeue` always takes the head; if either fails, claude-code is `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6) until an adapter with a traceable key exists, recorded in the feature matrix.

162: ## Execution organization (operator, 2026-10-11): four phases, then parallel domain coding
163: 
164: Operator directive (verbatim): "I want the implementation plan to be organized into requirements as a phase, interfaces and code stubs as a phase for the entire plan, test-driven development unit tests with mocks as a single phase, and then you can begin implementation coding in a domain-driven design breakdown so that agents can be run in parallel for the coding."
165: 
166: Precedence: this section fixes the execution order, phase gates, hostile-validation points, and TODOs for the whole plan. The sections "Scope catalog: Phase A", "Scope catalog: Phase B", and "Scope catalog: Phase C" (formerly the per-slice phases) and the P0 steps define scope, contracts, named tests, gates, and acceptance only; wherever they describe per-slice ordering, per-slice TODO transitions, or per-slice HV, this section governs. Each slice text is delivered through the phases below: its "Contract" part in Phase 2, its "RED" and "Mocks-green" parts in Phase 3, and its "Real" part, integration gates, and live checks in Phase 4 under the bounded context that owns its files.
167: 
168: Prerequisites (before Phase 1, each under its own TODO and the BDPv4 loop, then their own HV): the P0.1 baseline (every pre-existing failure fixed, zero failures and zero skips, including the Windows findings), P0.0a (REPL `generateDocument` validator), P0.1a (Nuke `Test` parameters, `TestPluginCore`, `TestAgentPlugins`; TR-MCP-NUKE-011..013), P0.1b (bats cases ported to Pester, `MAINT-BATSTOPESTER-001`; operator, 2026-10-11, PowerShell-only ruling), and P0.1c (Build.Tests removed from `MigrationIntegrationTests`, TR-MCP-NUKE-014), because every later gate runs through those Nuke targets and Pester is the only plugin test runner.
169: 
170: Phase 1: Requirements (entire plan). P0 steps 1-9 as written, with the TODO list of P0 step 8 replaced by the phase and domain TODOs below. Output: every FR, TR, TEST, AC, mapping, and use case of the catalog (Phases A, B, and C) in the store and in this plan; the agent-context catalog completed from the architecture document section 6; the feature matrix rows from P0.2. Exit: G5 phase-exit rule, then the phase HV of requirements, then operator approval.
171: 
172: Phase 2: Interfaces and code stubs (entire plan). Every contract named by the scope catalog and the architecture document, as compiling code whose members return neutral values (empty, null, false; never throwing) so Phase 3 tests fail on assertions:
173: - CQRS: every command and query record and its handler stub (one per unit of work), registered by `AddCqrsHandlers`; every policy interface and stub (TerminalTurnOutcomeGuard, RequestClassification, HvVerdictMapping, CompletionGate); every service seam the slices name (for example `ISessionLogRequestIdMinter`, `ISessionTurnCompletionGate`, `IAgentContextCandidateSource`, `IWorkspaceCommitReader`).
174: - Shared files that parallel agents must not edit later, completed here in full: new entity classes and their `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` classes as compiling, unregistered seams (no `DbSet`, no registration in `McpDbContext`, and no new property on an existing entity: `McpDbContext.cs:301-308` ignores the pending-model-changes warning, so a registered model change without its migration would make queries select columns the database lacks and regress the existing tests that call `Migrate()`, 62 call sites in `tests/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests`; the registered model change, the migrations, and the S3 backfill are real schema behavior and belong to the Phase 4 context StorageSchema, after their Phase 3 RED tests); `McpClientJsonContext` registrations; DTOs and their client mirrors; `GenericClientPassthrough` allow-list, `ClientMutationPolicy`, and `ReplYamlMessageValidator` registrations; DI in `Program.cs` and `McpStdioHost.cs`; `appsettings.yaml` sections and options classes with validation; the golden contract files `docs/context/session-turn-review-contract.json` and `docs/context/agent-context-contract.json`.
175: - Surfaces complete (they only dispatch): controllers and routes with their aliases, MCP tools, typed client methods, REPL methods; plugin function and tool signatures (PowerShell functions returning `$null`, `$false`, or `@()`; each TypeScript host adapter in its final forwarding form, because it holds no logic); Nuke target skeletons named by the catalog.
176: Exit: `./build.ps1 Compile`, G2 shows no regression of existing tests, G4 and G6 still green for existing suites, the stubs listed against the catalog, then the phase HV of interfaces, then operator approval.
177: 
178: Phase 3: Test-driven unit tests with mocks (single phase, entire plan). Every unit test the scope catalog names, written from the ACs, run RED against the Phase 2 stubs (the RED receipt: command, counts, first assertion per test class), then made green against mocks only (contract tests with an oracle double and permanent mutant tests; NSubstitute or hand-written doubles; Pester `Mock`), each with its recorded negative check (a wrong mock fails the target test). Also the golden-contract tests and the documentation contract tests. Integration suites (G3), `PluginSessionLogIntegration`, and live checks are not part of this phase. Exit: every Phase 3 test green against mocks with zero skips, the RED and negative-check receipts, then the phase HV of tests, then operator approval.
179: 
180: Phase 4: Implementation by bounded context, coding agents in parallel. Each context below is one work package with one coding agent, its own branch from the Phase 3 head, and its own TODO; contexts run in parallel where their dependencies allow. Because Phase 2 completed every shared file, each agent edits only the files its context owns; an agent that needs a change outside its context stops and raises it for a Phase 2 amendment. Each agent turns its context's Phase 3 tests green against the real implementation (no test weakened), adds its integration tests, runs its gates with zero failures and zero skips, and ends with its own domain HV. After all contexts merge: G1-G6 on Linux (LAB-OMARCHY) and Windows (PAYTON-LEGION2 through the WSMan route), `PluginSessionLogIntegration`, the live checks of "End-to-end verification", the phase-wide HV, and operator approval.

Write the HV brief: the claims (with commands, paths, test counts, SHAs, session turn ids), the untrusted implementer receipt, the acceptance rule, mandatory surfaces A-D, the add-profile first action, the review-only scope, and the receipt paths.
228: - Launch the reviewer with `codex exec -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort="max" --sandbox workspace-write -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true -C <worktree> --json -`, brief on stdin. The reviewer is review-only (it writes only under `docs/receipts/hv/` and to its own MCP session-log turn) and returns claim-by-claim PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN, `OverallVerdict`, accuracy, completeness, findings, and a `=== VERDICT JSON ===` block. The implementing agent writes the brief and launches the run; it never edits the reviewer's output or verdict. Verify the live model and effort from the Codex session rollout (`turn_context` with `model=gpt-6-astra`, `effort=max`); a run on any other model or effort is not an HV. 229: - Receipts: the runner writes `docs/receipts/hv/<utc>-<gate>.request.jsonl` (a meta object with the launch command, model, effort, head SHA, and brief SHA-256, plus the full brief body; built from PowerShell objects with `ConvertTo-Json -Compress`) and `.response.jsonl` (the reviewer's complete `--json` event stream), and, after the reviewer completes, `.rollout.jsonl` (a copy of the completed reviewer thread's Codex rollout file, which records its runtime `turn_context`; the agent-context `runtime_identity` check reads it). 71: ## 3. Cross-cutting conventions

73: - Workspace scoping: every request is scoped to one workspace through the `X-Workspace-Path` header (REST), the `workspacePath` parameter (MCP tools, REPL), or `MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH` (plugins). Every stored record carries its `WorkspaceId`, and no read ever crosses workspaces.
74: - Authentication: `X-Api-Key` (or `api_key`) from the workspace marker. Plugins never call REST directly; they use the REPL wrapper.
75: - Plugin scripting: PowerShell only (operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."). `plugins/core/lib-ps` is the one plugin core for all nine hosts; cline, cline-v2, and opencode keep only the adapter entry file their host API forces, which forwards each host hook invocation (`{ input, output }`) to `lib/plugin-hook.ps1 -HostEvent` and applies the returned `output`, forwards each tool call (`{ params, hostContext }`) to `lib/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 -InvocationFromStdin`, and registers the tools listed in `lib/tool-descriptors.json`; the host's own build compiles that one file into the git-ignored `dist/`; Pester is the only plugin test runner.
76: - Routes: every REST route exists under `/qbrainai/...` with the legacy alias `/mcpserver/...`.
77: - Errors: every REST error of a unit this plan adds or changes is the `ClassifiedError` problem+json body `{ "type", "title", "status", "detail", "code", "message", "retryable", "details" }` emitted through `McpErrorClassifier` (`SessionLogController.cs` and the agent-context controller); `code` carries the unit's error code (for example `review_status_conflict`, `agent_context_budget_exceeded`), the HTTP status is the one stated per unit (400 validation, 403 not allowed, 404 not found, 409 conflict or disabled, 422 semantic refusal), and MCP tools return `{ code, error, message, retryable, details }`. Existing routes whose behavior this plan does not change keep today's error bodies (for example the `{ error }` 400 of the dialog route and the "Invalid session identifier." problem of the open and title routes), stated per unit. The REPL error envelope is `type: error` with `code`, `message`, and `retryable`.

17: 1. One user request is exactly one session-log turn, minted by the server when the message arrives, and every write lands on the turn of the request that caused it (Phase A).
18: 2. Every turn carries a request class and two review records (agent and hostile) with lossless decimal scores, a status lifecycle, configurable thresholds, and a server-enforced completion gate (Phase B).
19: 3. Every agent invocation can run stateless: the server builds a bounded, reproducible context package from the profile, rules, requirements, session-log evidence, trusted prior responses, and current code, and only responses graded at 98/98 with no FAIL or UNKNOWN become trusted context for later requests (Phase C).
20: 
21: The agent-context scope depends on the turn-logging scope (turns are the unit a package is built for, and session-log turns are evidence) and on the review scope (the thresholds and the 98/98 grading rule). Phases A, B, and C name scope areas; execution runs in four phases across all three (section 8): requirements, interfaces and code stubs, test-driven unit tests with mocks, and implementation by bounded context with parallel coding agents.

71: ## 3. Cross-cutting conventions
72: 
73: - Workspace scoping: every request is scoped to one workspace through the `X-Workspace-Path` header (REST), the `workspacePath` parameter (MCP tools, REPL), or `MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH` (plugins). Every stored record carries its `WorkspaceId`, and no read ever crosses workspaces.
74: - Authentication: `X-Api-Key` (or `api_key`) from the workspace marker. Plugins never call REST directly; they use the REPL wrapper.
75: - Plugin scripting: PowerShell only (operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."). `plugins/core/lib-ps` is the one plugin core for all nine hosts; cline, cline-v2, and opencode keep only the adapter entry file their host API forces, which forwards each host hook invocation (`{ input, output }`) to `lib/plugin-hook.ps1 -HostEvent` and applies the returned `output`, forwards each tool call (`{ params, hostContext }`) to `lib/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 -InvocationFromStdin`, and registers the tools listed in `lib/tool-descriptors.json`; the host's own build compiles that one file into the git-ignored `dist/`; Pester is the only plugin test runner.
76: - Routes: every REST route exists under `/qbrainai/...` with the legacy alias `/mcpserver/...`.
77: - Errors: every REST error of a unit this plan adds or changes is the `ClassifiedError` problem+json body `{ "type", "title", "status", "detail", "code", "message", "retryable", "details" }` emitted through `McpErrorClassifier` (`SessionLogController.cs` and the agent-context controller); `code` carries the unit's error code (for example `review_status_conflict`, `agent_context_budget_exceeded`), the HTTP status is the one stated per unit (400 validation, 403 not allowed, 404 not found, 409 conflict or disabled, 422 semantic refusal), and MCP tools return `{ code, error, message, retryable, details }`. The completion gate is the one exception to the code rule: its `code` is `validation_error` and its message starts with the token `session_turn_completion_gate` followed by the missing items in the order requestClass, agentReview, hostileReview (FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC006); the diagrams name that refusal by its token. Existing routes whose behavior this plan does not change keep today's error bodies (for example the `{ error }` 400 of the dialog route and the "Invalid session identifier." problem of the open and title routes), stated per unit. The REPL error envelope is `type: error` with `code`, `message`, and `retryable`.
78: - Identifiers: every identifier is human-readable and meaningful (operator, 2026-10-11: "Please use human-readable, meaningful identifiers."). Session ids `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`; server-minted request ids `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>`; agent-context record keys derive from the turn and session they belong to (section 6.3): packages `pkg-<requestId>-<nn>`, responses `rsp-<requestId>-<nn>`, grades `grd-<responseId>-<kind>-<nn>`, relationships `rel-<type>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<nn>`, HV requests `hvr-<sessionId>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>`. Document labels use the command, query, process, and policy names.
79: - Root ids: every record carries the root ids of its parents (workspace, MCP session, request, and for agent context the package and response).
80: - Secrets: no API key, token, password, or credential is ever stored in a turn field, a context package, or a response; the session-log sanitizer and the agent-context secret filter redact on write and on every read surface.
81: - Process: the plan runs in the four execution phases of section 8 under the Byrd Development Process v4 (requirements, tests red, mocks green, implementation green, full gates with zero failures and zero skips); each prerequisite, the end of Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3, each bounded context at the end of its Phase 4 work package, and the phase-wide Phase 4 HV end with a Codex gpt-6-astra max hostile validation at accuracy and completeness of at least 98 with every claim PASS. Builds and tests run as Nuke targets natively on Windows or Linux; GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines are not part of any requirement or process; Octopus (container on LAB-OMARCHY) is used only for releases.

83: ## 4. Phase A: correct, independent turn logging
84:

87: - Server: `SessionLogService.SubmitWithOutcomesAsync` (per-turn outcomes), `ISessionLogService.MintTurnAsync`, `ISessionLogRequestIdMinter`, `ISessionLogTurnUpsertGuard`, `SessionLogTurnEntity.IngressNonce` (unique filtered index on (WorkspaceId, SessionLogId, IngressNonce) where not null, and a second unique filtered index on (WorkspaceId, RequestId) where IngressNonce is not null, so minted request ids are unique across the workspace's sessions while legacy rows are untouched; TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-006).
88: - PowerShell plugin core (`plugins/core/lib-ps`): prompt hook, arrival bridge (claude-code, claude-cowork), `Sync-PluginArrivalLog`, verb binding (`New-ReplInvocationBinding`, `Resolve-ReplTargetTurn`), truthful persist (`Get-ReplTurnWriteOutcome`, `Invoke-ReplPersistTurn`), failsafe and alias journal, Stop gate (`Get-PluginStopGateTurns`, pure `Get-PluginStopGateFindings`).

90: - Plugin per-host-session state (one directory per host session key under the plugin cache):
91:   - `turns/<requestId>.yaml` with its own lock `turns/<requestId>.lock`: one file per turn.
92:   - `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/turn-state.yaml`: `writeTarget { requestId, deliveredAtUtc, source }`, `openDelivered [requestId]`, `queue [{ kind, requestId, nonce, enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state, stateOffset, mintedAtUtc }]`, `appliedThroughOffset`, `mcpSessionId`, `ledger [...]`, `unsupportedSince { causeOffset, causeOperation, reason }`; every entry carries the root ids; written by one atomic replace under `turn-open.lock`.
93:   - `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/ended.yaml` (`reason: session_end`), `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/aliases.yaml` (alias journal), `sessions/<key>/arrival-bridge.pid`.
94:   - `current-turn.yaml` is a read-only legacy status file and is never used for targeting.

96: Request lifecycle (plugin queue entry):
97: 
98: ```mermaid
99: stateDiagram-v2
100:     [*] --> queued: enqueue (mint)
101:     queued --> delivered: dequeue of head, or remove with absorbed_mid_turn
102:     queued --> withdrawn: remove with another or no reason, or popAll
103:     delivered --> closed: completeTurn or failTurn confirmed by server
104:     withdrawn --> closed: failTurn "withdrawn before delivery" confirmed
105:     closed --> [*]
106: ```

108: ### 4.2 Units of work (CQRS handlers)
109: 
110: Each unit of work is exactly one CQRS command or query with its handler (operator, 2026-10-11: "I want to be clear, unit of work maps to one CQRS handler"), following `QBrainAi.Cqrs`: a `sealed record` implementing `ICommand<TResult>` or `IQuery<TResult>` and its handler in the same file under `src/QBrainAi.Services/<Area>/Commands` or `Queries`, registered by `AddCqrsHandlers`, returning `Result<TResult>`; controllers and MCP tools dispatch through `IDispatcher.SendAsync` or `QueryAsync` and map failures through `McpErrorClassifier`. Phase A and B handlers delegate to the `ISessionLogService` members the plan names.
111: 
112: #### MintSessionTurnCommand: mint a turn at ingress [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001]
113: 
114: - Handler: `MintSessionTurnCommand(string WorkspacePath, string Agent, string SessionId, SessionLogMintTurnRequest Request) : ICommand<SessionLogMintTurnResult>` and `MintSessionTurnCommandHandler` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/SessionLog/Commands/MintSessionTurnCommand.cs`, delegating to `ISessionLogService.MintTurnAsync`.
115: - Trigger: a user message arrives at a host arrival mechanism (prompt hook, arrival bridge, or host-native adapter). Only hooks and adapters call it; there is no MCP tool, and the plugin wrapper refuses a model-originated call with `mint_requires_host_ingress`.
116: - Surfaces: `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint` (alias `/mcpserver/...`), client `MintTurnAsync`, REPL `workflow.sessionlog.mintTurn`.
117: - Request `SessionLogMintTurnRequest`: `ingressNonce` (string, required: the host's per-message id or a SHA-256 of host event fields), `queryTitle`, `queryText`, `model`, `planFile` (value or the `None` sentinel), `todoId` (value or `None`).
118: - Response `SessionLogMintTurnResult`: `requestId` (`req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>`), `outcome` (`created` or `merged`), and `storedStatus` on `merged` only (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-005).
119:   - 201 `{ requestId, outcome: "created" }`: a new in-progress turn.
120:   - 200 `{ requestId, outcome: "merged", storedStatus }`: the same nonce was already minted in this MCP session; the same `requestId` is returned and a terminal turn is not reopened.
121: - Errors: 400 `ingress_nonce_invalid` (missing or invalid nonce, TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-005), 400 `validation_error` (invalid `planFile` or `todoId`), 404 with detail code `session_not_open`, 500 with final detail code `mint_collision_exhausted` after six request-id collisions.
122: 
123: ```mermaid
124: flowchart TD
125:     S(["Mint request received"]) --> NV{"ingressNonce present and valid?"}
126:     NV -->|no| E400N(["400 ingress_nonce_invalid"])
127:     NV -->|yes| V{"planFile and todoId valid?"}
128:     V -->|no| E400(["400 validation_error"])
129:     V -->|yes| O{"MCP session open for agent and sessionId?"}
130:     O -->|no| E404(["404 session_not_open"])
131:     O -->|yes| N{"Turn with this ingressNonce exists in the session?"}
132:     N -->|yes| M(["200 merged: existing requestId and storedStatus, status unchanged"])
133:     N -->|no| K["attempt = 1"]
134:     K --> G["Minter generates req-UTC-8hex"]
135:     G --> I["Insert in-progress turn with ingressNonce"]
136:     I --> R{"Insert result"}
137:     R -->|success| C(["201 created: requestId"])
138:     R -->|nonce unique index violated by a concurrent mint| X["Read the turn that holds the nonce"]
139:     X --> M
140:     R -->|requestId unique index violated| A{"attempt less than 6?"}
141:     A -->|yes| B["attempt = attempt + 1"]
142:     B --> G
143:     A -->|no| E500(["500 mint_collision_exhausted"])
144: ```
145: 
146: #### SubmitSessionLogCommand: submit a session log with per-turn outcomes [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004]
147: 
148: - Handler: `SubmitSessionLogCommand(string WorkspacePath, UnifiedSessionLogDto Log) : ICommand<SessionLogSubmitResult>` and `SubmitSessionLogCommandHandler` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/SessionLog/Commands/SubmitSessionLogCommand.cs`, delegating to `ISessionLogService.SubmitWithOutcomesAsync` and applying, per turn, policy TerminalTurnOutcomeGuard, policy RequestClassification when the turn carries `requestClass`, and policy CompletionGate when the write moves the turn to `completed` or `failed` (from S10).
149: - Surfaces: `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog` (existing route), MCP `sessionlog_submit`, client `SubmitAsync`, REPL submit. This is the route every turn verb already uses: the plugin verbs `appendActions`, `appendDecisions`, `updateTurn`, `completeTurn`, and `failTurn` send the one bound turn in a session document (`Invoke-ReplPersistTurn`, `plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1:1602-1736`, method `client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync`; process PersistTurnWriteWithReceipt), and so do the REPL workflow (`src/QBrainAi.Repl.Core/SessionLogWorkflow.cs`) and McpAgent (`src/QBrainAi.McpAgent/SessionLog/SessionLogWorkflow.cs`). Dialog and titles use their own routes (AppendTurnDialogCommand, SetTurnTitleCommand, SetSessionTitleCommand).
150: - Request: the unified session-log document (`UnifiedSessionLogDto`) with its turns.
151: - Response 201 `SessionLogSubmitResult`: existing fields plus `turns: [{ requestId, outcome, storedStatus, reason }]`, where `outcome` is `created`, `merged`, or `skipped_terminal`. MCP returns `{ success, id, turns }`. The status code stays 201.
152: - Rules: an identical resubmit is `merged` with reason `no_change`; duplicate request ids in one submission apply last-wins with one outcome each; a write whose status would move a terminal turn (the stored status is terminal, that is `completed`, `failed`, `closed`, `canceled`, or `cancelled` (`IsTerminalTurnStatus`), the incoming status is supplied and differs from it, and either the incoming status is not terminal or the write is a superseded hook persist; today's guard at `SessionLogService.cs:1611-1618`, which the seam `ISessionLogTurnUpsertGuard` replaces unchanged, TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-002) is `skipped_terminal` and changes nothing, while a write that omits the status merges additively even on a terminal turn (omitted-status enrichment, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC003); there is no `skipped_duplicate` outcome.
153: - Errors: 400 `validation_error`; 400 `request_class_invalid`; 400 `validation_error` with the token `session_turn_completion_gate` (from S10: one or more turns of the submission move to `completed` or `failed` without meeting the gate; every turn is evaluated first, then the whole submission is rejected atomically and the error names each failing `requestId` with its missing items, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC005).
154: 
155: ```mermaid
156: flowchart TD
157:     S(["Submit received"]) --> P{"Document parses?"}
158:     P -->|no| E400(["400 validation_error"])
159:     P -->|yes| D["Collapse duplicate requestIds last-wins"]
160:     D --> L["For each turn in the submission"]
161:     L --> F{"Turn exists in store?"}
162:     F -->|no| CR["Insert turn: outcome created"]
163:     F -->|yes| T{"Policy TerminalTurnOutcomeGuard: stored status terminal, incoming status supplied and different, and either not terminal or a superseded hook persist?"}
164:     T -->|yes| SK["Leave stored turn unchanged: outcome skipped_terminal with storedStatus and reason"]
165:     T -->|no| Q{"Incoming equals stored?"}
166:     Q -->|yes| NC["outcome merged, reason no_change"]
167:     Q -->|no| MG["Merge fields additively: outcome merged"]
168:     CR --> RC{"Turn carries requestClass?"}
169:     MG --> RC
170:     RC -->|yes| PC["Policy RequestClassification: normalize, Chore flip on an in-progress turn"]
171:     PC --> PCV{"Class valid?"}
172:     PCV -->|no| E3(["400 request_class_invalid: change tracker cleared, nothing saved"])
173:     PCV -->|yes| TRN
174:     RC -->|no| TRN{"Write moves the turn to completed or failed?"}
175:     TRN -->|yes| GT["Policy CompletionGate (from S10)"]
176:     GT --> GTR{"Gate met?"}
177:     GTR -->|no| FL["Record this requestId and its missing items as a gate failure"]
178:     FL --> NX
179:     GTR -->|yes| NX
180:     TRN -->|no| NX{"More turns?"}
181:     SK --> NX
182:     NC --> NX
183:     NX -->|yes| L
184:     NX -->|no| AF{"Any gate failure recorded?"}
185:     AF -->|yes| E4(["400 validation_error session_turn_completion_gate naming each failing requestId and its missing items: change tracker cleared, nothing saved"])
186:     AF -->|no| SV["Save changes in one transaction"]
187:     SV --> R(["201 with turns outcome list"])
188: ```
189: 
190: #### UpsertSessionTurnCommand: append or merge one turn [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007]
191: 
192: The single-turn routes (this unit, PatchSessionTurnCommand, ReplaceSessionTurnCommand, CompleteSessionTurnCommand, FailSessionTurnCommand) keep today's request bodies, response bodies, and errors (`SessionLogController.cs:191-220` and `:425-566`, `SessionLogService.cs:716-889`). They are the explicit route for deliberate status corrections (the comment on the submit guard, `SessionLogService.cs:1610`), so policy TerminalTurnOutcomeGuard does not apply to them and they report no per-turn outcome. This plan adds only the Phase B policies to them: RequestClassification when a write carries `requestClass` (S4), and CompletionGate when a write moves the turn into `completed` or `failed`, or a PUT carries a terminal status (S10, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC003, AC004). Both refusals reach these routes through `McpErrorClassifier` (S5, TR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002 AC-003) as `ClassifiedError` bodies; every other error keeps today's body.
193: 
194: - Handler: `UpsertSessionTurnCommand(string WorkspacePath, string Agent, string SessionId, UnifiedRequestEntryDto Turn) : ICommand<long>` and `UpsertSessionTurnCommandHandler` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/SessionLog/Commands/UpsertSessionTurnCommand.cs`, delegating to `ISessionLogService.UpsertTurnAsync` (`SessionLogService.cs:716-806`), which returns the turn id; the controller composes today's body.
195: - Surfaces: `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/turn` (alias `/mcpserver/...`), client `UpsertTurnAsync(agent, sessionId, UnifiedRequestEntryDto)` returning `SessionLogTurnSubmitResult`, REPL `client.SessionLog.UpsertTurnAsync`; no MCP tool (MCP callers write turns through `sessionlog_submit`, SubmitSessionLogCommand). The plugin, REPL-workflow, and McpAgent verbs do not use this route; they persist through SubmitSessionLogCommand.
196: - Request: `UnifiedRequestEntryDto` (the turn with its `requestId`; from Phase B also `requestClass`). A new turn is inserted with its turn context (planFile and todoId validated as for a new entry); an existing turn is merged additively (omitted fields never clobber stored values), whatever its status.
197: - Response 201 `{ turnId, agent, sessionId, requestId }` (Location `/qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}`). A first insert that loses a unique-index race to a concurrent insert of the same requestId is retried once as an update of the winning row.
198: - Errors: 400 problem "Invalid turn body." (no body); 400 problem "Invalid turn payload." 204:     BD -->|yes| ID{"Session id and request id valid?"}

210:     NEW -->|no| E3(["400 problem Invalid turn payload."])
211:     NEW -->|yes| INS["Insert the new turn"]
212:     EX -->|yes| CTX{"Supplied planFile and todoId valid, filesModified and commits attributed to the workspace?"}
213:     CTX -->|no| E4(["400 problem Invalid turn payload."])
214:     CTX -->|yes| MG["Merge additively, whatever the stored status: omitted fields never clobber stored values"]
215:     INS --> RC{"requestClass supplied (from S4)?"}
216:     MG --> RC
217:     RC -->|yes| PC["Policy RequestClassification"]
218:     PC --> PCV{"Class valid?"}
219:     PCV -->|no| E5(["400 request_class_invalid: nothing saved"])
220:     PCV -->|yes| TRN
221:     RC -->|no| TRN{"Write moves the turn into completed or failed (from S10)?"}
222:     TRN -->|yes| GT["Policy CompletionGate"]
223:     GT --> GTR{"Gate met?"}
224:     GTR -->|no| E6(["400 validation_error session_turn_completion_gate with missing items: change tracker cleared, nothing saved"])

226:     TRN -->|no| QB{"Terminal QBAgent turn without a decision, action, or commit (ValidateTerminalTurnCompliance)?"}

232:     RACE -->|no| R(["201 turnId, agent, sessionId, requestId"])

71: ## 3. Cross-cutting conventions
72: 
73: - Workspace scoping: every request is scoped to one workspace through the `X-Workspace-Path` header (REST), the `workspacePath` parameter (MCP tools, REPL), or `MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH` (plugins). Every stored record carries its `WorkspaceId`, and no read ever crosses workspaces.
74: - Authentication: `X-Api-Key` (or `api_key`) from the workspace marker. Plugins never call REST directly; they use the REPL wrapper.
75: - Plugin scripting: PowerShell only (operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."). `plugins/core/lib-ps` is the one plugin core for all nine hosts; cline, cline-v2, and opencode keep only the adapter entry file their host API forces, which forwards each host hook invocation (`{ input, output }`) to `lib/plugin-hook.ps1 -HostEvent` and applies the returned `output`, forwards each tool call (`{ params, hostContext }`) to `lib/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 -InvocationFromStdin`, and registers the tools listed in `lib/tool-descriptors.json`; the host's own build compiles that one file into the git-ignored `dist/`; Pester is the only plugin test runner.
76: - Routes: every REST route exists under `/qbrainai/...` with the legacy alias `/mcpserver/...`.
77: - Errors: every REST error of a unit this plan adds or changes is the `ClassifiedError` problem+json body `{ "type", "title", "status", "detail", "code", "message", "retryable", "details" }` emitted through `McpErrorClassifier` (`SessionLogController.cs` and the agent-context controller); `code` carries the unit's error code (for example `review_status_conflict`, `agent_context_budget_exceeded`), the HTTP status is the one stated per unit (400 validation, 403 not allowed, 404 not found, 409 conflict or disabled, 422 semantic refusal), and MCP tools return `{ code, error, message, retryable, details }`. The completion gate is the one exception to the code rule: its `code` is `validation_error` and its message starts with the token `session_turn_completion_gate` followed by the missing items in the order requestClass, agentReview, hostileReview (FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC006); the diagrams name that refusal by its token. Existing routes whose behavior this plan does not change keep today's error bodies (for example the `{ error }` 400 of the dialog route and the "Invalid session identifier." problem of the open and title routes), stated per unit. The REPL error envelope is `type: error` with `code`, `message`, and `retryable`.
78: - Identifiers: every identifier is human-readable and meaningful (operator, 2026-10-11: "Please use human-readable, meaningful identifiers."). Session ids `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`; server-minted request ids `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>`; agent-context record keys derive from the turn and session they belong to (section 6.3): packages `pkg-<requestId>-<nn>`, responses `rsp-<requestId>-<nn>`, grades `grd-<responseId>-<kind>-<nn>`, relationships `rel-<type>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<nn>`, HV requests `hvr-<sessionId>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>`. Document labels use the command, query, process, and policy names.
79: - Root ids: every record carries the root ids of its parents (workspace, MCP session, request, and for agent context the package and response).
80: - Secrets: no API key, token, password, or credential is ever stored in a turn field, a context package, or a response; the session-log sanitizer and the agent-context secret filter redact on write and on every read surface.
81: - Process: the plan runs in the four execution phases of section 8 under the Byrd Development Process v4 (requirements, tests red, mocks green, implementation green, full gates with zero failures and zero skips); each prerequisite, the end of Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3, each bounded context at the end of its Phase 4 work package, and the phase-wide Phase 4 HV end with a Codex gpt-6-astra max hostile validation at accuracy and completeness of at least 98 with every claim PASS. Builds and tests run as Nuke targets natively on Windows or Linux; GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines are not part of any requirement or process; Octopus (container on LAB-OMARCHY) is used only for releases.

460: #### Policy TerminalTurnOutcomeGuard: terminal-turn outcome guard (`ISessionLogTurnUpsertGuard`) [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004]
461: 
462: Applied by SubmitSessionLogCommand only, as today: the single-turn routes (UpsertSessionTurnCommand, PatchSessionTurnCommand, ReplaceSessionTurnCommand, CompleteSessionTurnCommand, FailSessionTurnCommand) are the explicit route for deliberate status corrections and have no outcome guard (`SessionLogService.cs:1610`). The seam replaces the inline guard at `SessionLogService.cs:1606-1618` without changing its rule (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-002): a write is skipped only when the stored status is terminal and the incoming status is supplied, differs from it, and is either not terminal or carried by a superseded hook persist; a write that omits the status, a review-section write, and a requestClass-only write merge on a terminal turn (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC003, AC004).

460: #### Policy TerminalTurnOutcomeGuard: terminal-turn outcome guard (`ISessionLogTurnUpsertGuard`) [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004]
461: 
462: Applied by SubmitSessionLogCommand only, as today: the single-turn routes (UpsertSessionTurnCommand, PatchSessionTurnCommand, ReplaceSessionTurnCommand, CompleteSessionTurnCommand, FailSessionTurnCommand) are the explicit route for deliberate status corrections and have no outcome guard (`SessionLogService.cs:1610`). It never saves; it returns the outcome the handler must honor. The seam replaces the inline guard at `SessionLogService.cs:1606-1618` without changing its rule (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-002): a write is skipped only when the stored status is terminal and the incoming status is supplied, differs from it, and is either not terminal or carried by a superseded hook persist; a write that omits the status, a review-section write, and a requestClass-only write merge on a terminal turn (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC003, AC004).

1338: ## 5. Phase B: request class, review records, thresholds
1339: 
1340: ### 5.1 Data model
1341: 
1342: - `SessionLogTurnEntity` gains `RequestClass` (16, indexed) and, per review kind (agent, hostile): `Status` (16, required), `OtherNotes` (text), `Correctness`, `Completeness`, `CorrectnessThreshold`, `CompletenessThreshold` (decimal, precision 29 scale 28), `Reviewer` (256), `ReviewedAt` (UTC), `RequestJsonlPath`, `ResponseJsonlPath` (2048).
1343: - Child `SessionLogTurnReviewReasonEntity { Id, WorkspaceId, SessionLogTurnId, Kind, Ordinal, Value }`.
1344: - Backfill: `RequestClass = Unclassified`, both review statuses `Unstarted`, on every existing row including soft-deleted rows.
1345: - Wire shape on `UnifiedRequestEntryDto`: `requestClass` and the two review objects `agentReview`, `hostileReview` with `status`, `otherNotes`, `correctness`, `completeness`, `correctnessThreshold`, `completenessThreshold`, `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`, `requestJsonlPath`, `responseJsonlPath`; unset fields are emitted as `null`.
1346: - Request classes: `Code`, `Docs`, `Chore` (case-insensitive in, PascalCase out); `Unclassified` exists only for legacy rows.
1347: - Review statuses: `Unnecessary`, `Unstarted`, `Running`, `Pass`, `Fail`, `Other`; `Unnecessary` and `Unstarted` are server-managed, and a review body naming either is refused with `review_unnecessary_not_client_writable` (FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-006-AC004, case `ReviewController_ClientCannotWriteUnstarted`).
1348: - Thresholds: `Mcp:SessionLog:ReviewThresholds:{Agent|Hostile}:{Correctness|Completeness}`, decimal in [0,1], default 0.98, inclusive, per instance through `McpInstanceResolver`.
1349: 
1350: ```mermaid
1351: stateDiagram-v2
1352:     [*] --> Unstarted: turn created
1353:     Unstarted --> Unnecessary: hostile only, class set to Chore on an in-progress turn
1354:     Unnecessary --> Unstarted: class changes away from Chore while still Unnecessary
1355:     Unstarted --> Running: review started (reviewer required)
1356:     Unstarted --> Pass: scores meet both thresholds
1357:     Unstarted --> Fail: a score below its threshold
1358:     Unstarted --> Other: otherNotes required
1359:     Running --> Pass
1360:     Running --> Fail
1361:     Running --> Other
1362:     Pass --> Pass: latest write wins
1363:     Pass --> Fail
1364:     Fail --> Pass
1365:     Pass --> Other
1366:     Fail --> Other
1367:     Other --> Pass
1368:     Other --> Fail
1369:     Running --> Unstarted: section reset on a nonterminal turn
1370:     Pass --> Unstarted: section reset on a nonterminal turn
1371:     Fail --> Unstarted: section reset on a nonterminal turn
1372:     Other --> Unstarted: section reset on a nonterminal turn
1373:     Pass --> Unnecessary: hostile section reset on a nonterminal Chore turn
1374:     Fail --> Unnecessary: hostile section reset on a nonterminal Chore turn
1375:     Other --> Unnecessary: hostile section reset on a nonterminal Chore turn
1376:     Running --> Unnecessary: hostile section reset on a nonterminal Chore turn
1377: ```
1378: 
1379: ### 5.2 Units of work (CQRS handlers)
1380: 
1381: The same rule as section 4.2: each unit is one command or query and its handler. Request classification and the completion gate are not units of their own; they are policies the turn write and close handlers (SubmitSessionLogCommand, the route every plugin, REPL-workflow, and McpAgent turn verb uses, and UpsertSessionTurnCommand, PatchSessionTurnCommand, ReplaceSessionTurnCommand, CompleteSessionTurnCommand, FailSessionTurnCommand) apply (section 5.3).
1382: 
1383: #### RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand: record a review [FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001, -002, -003, -004, -005, -006, -007, FR-SUPPORT-016]
1384: 
1385: - Handler: `RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand(string WorkspacePath, string Agent, string SessionId, string RequestId, SessionLogTurnReviewKind Kind, SessionLogTurnReviewInput Review) : ICommand<SessionLogTurnReviewDto>` and `RecordSessionTurnReviewCommandHandler` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/SessionLog/Commands/RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand.cs`, applying policy HvVerdictMapping when `hvVerdict` is supplied.
1386: - Surfaces: `PUT /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/{requestId}/sections/{section}` with section `agentReview` or `hostileReview` (aliases `agent-review`, `agent_review`, `hostile-review`, `hostile_review`, case-insensitive); MCP `sessionlog_record_review(agent, sessionId, requestId, kind, reviewJson, workspacePath)`; client `RecordTurnReviewAsync`; REPL and plugin `workflow.sessionlog.recordReview` (plugin also accepts `hvReceiptPath`, mapped locally; hostile kind accepts `hvVerdict`).
1387: - Request `SessionLogTurnReviewInput`: `status` (optional), `otherNotes`, `correctness`, `completeness` (JSON number or numeric string, lexeme `^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$`, at most 28 fractional digits, value in [0,1]), `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt` (UTC with offset), `requestJsonlPath`, `responseJsonlPath`, `hvVerdict` (hostile only: on an agent review it is refused with 400 `validation_error`, `details.field` `hvVerdict`). Thresholds on input are ignored.
1388: - Response: the turn's review record with server-derived status and stamped thresholds. Works on every turn status, including completed and failed turns.
1389: - Errors: 404 `not_found` (turn); 400 `validation_error` for an unknown section or `hvVerdict` on an agent review; 400 with the code: `review_invalid_status`, `review_unnecessary_not_client_writable`, `review_other_notes_not_allowed`, `review_other_notes_required`, `review_field_forbidden_for_status`, `review_field_required_for_status`, `review_score_out_of_range`, `review_receipt_paths_required`, `review_score_format`, `review_score_precision`, `review_field_too_long`, `review_timestamp_invalid`, `review_reason_blank`, 422 `review_status_conflict` (includes the thresholds in force and the derived status).
1390: 
1391: ```mermaid
1392: flowchart TD
1393:     S(["Review write received"]) --> SEC{"Section is agentReview or hostileReview or an alias?"}
1394:     SEC -->|no| E0(["400 validation_error unknown section"])
1395:     SEC -->|yes| TF{"Turn found in the session?"}
1396:     TF -->|no| E16(["404 not_found"])
1397:     TF -->|yes| LEX{"Score lexemes match the pattern, at most 28 fraction digits, value in 0..1?"}
1398:     LEX -->|format| E1(["400 review_score_format"])
1399:     LEX -->|precision| E2(["400 review_score_precision"])
1400:     LEX -->|range| E3(["400 review_score_out_of_range"])
1401:     LEX -->|ok| HV{"hvVerdict supplied?"}
1402:     HV -->|on an agent review| E17(["400 validation_error, details.field hvVerdict"])
1403:     HV -->|on a hostile review| MAP["Policy HvVerdictMapping: map the verdict to status, reasons, and otherNotes"]
1404:     HV -->|no| ST
1405:     MAP --> ST{"Status supplied?"}
1406:     ST -->|Unnecessary or Unstarted| E4(["400 review_unnecessary_not_client_writable"])
1407:     ST -->|not a known status| E5(["400 review_invalid_status"])
1408:     ST -->|omitted| DER{"Both scores present?"}
1409:     DER -->|no| E6(["400 review_field_required_for_status"])
1410:     DER -->|yes| DRV["Derive Pass or Fail against the thresholds in force"]
1411:     ST -->|Pass or Fail| CMP["Derive from scores against the thresholds in force"]
1412:     CMP --> CF{"Supplied status equals derived?"}
1413:     CF -->|no| E7(["422 review_status_conflict with thresholds and derived status"])
1414:     CF -->|yes| FLD

1338: ## 5. Phase B: request class, review records, thresholds
1339: 
1340: ### 5.1 Data model
1341: 
1342: - `SessionLogTurnEntity` gains `RequestClass` (16, indexed) and, per review kind (agent, hostile): `Status` (16, required), `OtherNotes` (text), `Correctness`, `Completeness`, `CorrectnessThreshold`, `CompletenessThreshold` (decimal, precision 29 scale 28), `Reviewer` (256), `ReviewedAt` (UTC), `RequestJsonlPath`, `ResponseJsonlPath` (2048).
1343: - Child `SessionLogTurnReviewReasonEntity { Id, WorkspaceId, SessionLogTurnId, Kind, Ordinal, Value }`.
1344: - Backfill: `RequestClass = Unclassified`, both review statuses `Unstarted`, on every existing row including soft-deleted rows.
1345: - Wire shape on `UnifiedRequestEntryDto`: `requestClass` and the two review objects `agentReview`, `hostileReview` with `status`, `otherNotes`, `correctness`, `completeness`, `correctnessThreshold`, `completenessThreshold`, `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`, `requestJsonlPath`, `responseJsonlPath`; unset fields are emitted as `null`.
1346: - Request classes: `Code`, `Docs`, `Chore` (case-insensitive in, PascalCase out); `Unclassified` exists only for legacy rows.
1347: - Review statuses: `Unnecessary`, `Unstarted`, `Running`, `Pass`, `Fail`, `Other`; `Unnecessary` and `Unstarted` are server-managed, and a review body naming either is refused with `review_unnecessary_not_client_writable` (FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-006-AC004, case `ReviewController_ClientCannotWriteUnstarted`).
1348: - Thresholds: `Mcp:SessionLog:ReviewThresholds:{Agent|Hostile}:{Correctness|Completeness}`, decimal in [0,1], default 0.98, inclusive, per instance through `McpInstanceResolver`.
1349: 
1350: ```mermaid
1351: stateDiagram-v2
1352:     [*] --> Unstarted: turn created
1353:     Unstarted --> Unnecessary: hostile only, class set to Chore on an in-progress turn
1354:     Unnecessary --> Unstarted: class changes away from Chore while still Unnecessary
1355:     Unstarted --> Running: review started (reviewer required)
1356:     Unstarted --> Pass: scores meet both thresholds
1357:     Unstarted --> Fail: a score below its threshold
1358:     Unstarted --> Other: otherNotes required
1359:     Running --> Pass
1360:     Running --> Fail
1361:     Running --> Other
1362:     Pass --> Pass: latest write wins
1363:     Pass --> Fail
1364:     Fail --> Pass
1365:     Pass --> Other
1366:     Fail --> Other
1367:     Other --> Pass
1368:     Other --> Fail
1369:     Running --> Unstarted: section reset on a nonterminal turn
1370:     Pass --> Unstarted: section reset on a nonterminal turn
1371:     Fail --> Unstarted: section reset on a nonterminal turn
1372:     Other --> Unstarted: section reset on a nonterminal turn
1373:     Pass --> Unnecessary: hostile section reset on a nonterminal Chore turn
1374:     Fail --> Unnecessary: hostile section reset on a nonterminal Chore turn
1375:     Other --> Unnecessary: hostile section reset on a nonterminal Chore turn
1376:     Running --> Unnecessary: hostile section reset on a nonterminal Chore turn
1377: ```
1378: 
1379: ### 5.2 Units of work (CQRS handlers)
1380: 
1381: The same rule as section 4.2: each unit is one command or query and its handler. Request classification and the completion gate are not units of their own; they are policies the turn write and close handlers (SubmitSessionLogCommand, the route every plugin, REPL-workflow, and McpAgent turn verb uses, and UpsertSessionTurnCommand, PatchSessionTurnCommand, ReplaceSessionTurnCommand, CompleteSessionTurnCommand, FailSessionTurnCommand) apply (section 5.3).
1382: 
1383: #### RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand: record a review [FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001, -002, -003, -004, -005, -006, -007, FR-SUPPORT-016]
1384: 
1385: - Handler: `RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand(string WorkspacePath, string Agent, string SessionId, string RequestId, SessionLogTurnReviewKind Kind, SessionLogTurnReviewInput Review) : ICommand<SessionLogTurnReviewDto>` and `RecordSessionTurnReviewCommandHandler` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/SessionLog/Commands/RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand.cs`, applying policy HvVerdictMapping when `hvVerdict` is supplied.
1386: - Surfaces: `PUT /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/{requestId}/sections/{section}` with section `agentReview` or `hostileReview` (aliases `agent-review`, `agent_review`, `hostile-review`, `hostile_review`, case-insensitive); MCP `sessionlog_record_review(agent, sessionId, requestId, kind, reviewJson, workspacePath)`; client `RecordTurnReviewAsync`; REPL and plugin `workflow.sessionlog.recordReview` (plugin also accepts `hvReceiptPath`, mapped locally; hostile kind accepts `hvVerdict`).
1387: - Request `SessionLogTurnReviewInput`: `status` (optional), `otherNotes`, `correctness`, `completeness` (JSON number or numeric string, lexeme `^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$`, at most 28 fractional digits, value in [0,1]), `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt` (UTC with offset), `requestJsonlPath`, `responseJsonlPath`, `hvVerdict` (hostile only: on an agent review it is refused with 400 `validation_error`, `details.field` `hvVerdict`). Thresholds on input are ignored.
1388: - Response: the turn's review record with server-derived status and stamped thresholds. Works on every turn status, including completed and failed turns.
1389: - Errors: 404 `not_found` (turn); 400 `validation_error` for an unknown section or `hvVerdict` on an agent review; 400 with the code: `review_invalid_status`, `review_unnecessary_not_client_writable`, `review_other_notes_not_allowed`, `review_other_notes_required`, `review_field_forbidden_for_status`, `review_field_required_for_status`, `review_score_out_of_range`, `review_receipt_paths_required`, `review_score_format`, `review_score_precision`, `review_field_too_long`, `review_timestamp_invalid`, `review_reason_blank`, 422 `review_status_conflict` (includes the thresholds in force and the derived status).
1390: 
1391: ```mermaid
1392: flowchart TD
1393:     S(["Review write received"]) --> SEC{"Section is agentReview or hostileReview or an alias?"}
1394:     SEC -->|no| E0(["400 validation_error unknown section"])
1395:     SEC -->|yes| TF{"Turn found in the session?"}
1396:     TF -->|no| E16(["404 not_found"])
1397:     TF -->|yes| LEX{"Score lexemes match the pattern, at most 28 fraction digits, value in 0..1?"}
1398:     LEX -->|format| E1(["400 review_score_format"])
1399:     LEX -->|precision| E2(["400 review_score_precision"])
1400:     LEX -->|range| E3(["400 review_score_out_of_range"])
1401:     LEX -->|ok| HV{"hvVerdict supplied?"}
1402:     HV -->|on an agent review| E17(["400 validation_error, details.field hvVerdict"])
1403:     HV -->|on a hostile review| MAP["Policy HvVerdictMapping: map the verdict to status, reasons, and otherNotes"]
1404:     HV -->|no| ST
1405:     MAP --> ST{"Status supplied?"}
1406:     ST -->|Unnecessary or Unstarted| E4(["400 review_unnecessary_not_client_writable"])
1407:     ST -->|not a known status| E5(["400 review_invalid_status"])
1408:     ST -->|omitted| DER{"Both scores present?"}
1409:     DER -->|no| E6(["400 review_field_required_for_status"])
1410:     DER -->|yes| DRV["Derive Pass or Fail against the thresholds in force"]
1411:     ST -->|Pass or Fail| CMP["Derive from scores against the thresholds in force"]
1412:     CMP --> CF{"Supplied status equals derived?"}
1413:     CF -->|no| E7(["422 review_status_conflict with thresholds and derived status"])
1414:     CF -->|yes| FLD
1415:     ST -->|Running or Other| FLD
1416:     DRV --> FLD{"Per-status fields valid?"}
1417:     FLD -->|forbidden field present| E8(["400 review_field_forbidden_for_status"])
1418:     FLD -->|required field missing| E9(["400 review_field_required_for_status"])
1419:     FLD -->|hostile Pass or Fail without both jsonl paths| E10(["400 review_receipt_paths_required"])
1420:     FLD -->|otherNotes text and status not Other| E11(["400 review_other_notes_not_allowed"])
1421:     FLD -->|Other with blank otherNotes| E12(["400 review_other_notes_required"])
1422:     FLD -->|blank reason| E13(["400 review_reason_blank"])
1423:     FLD -->|timestamp without offset| E14(["400 review_timestamp_invalid"])
1424:     FLD -->|field over its length| E15(["400 review_field_too_long"])
1425:     FLD -->|valid| SAN["Sanitize text fields"]
1426:     SAN --> STAMP["Stamp the thresholds in force"]
1427:     STAMP --> SAVE["Replace the record: latest write wins, any turn status"]
1428:     SAVE --> OK(["200 review record with derived status and stamped thresholds"])
1429: ```

1568: ### 5.4 Processes (plugin, REPL, and McpAgent)

1570: #### Process ConvertHvReceiptToReview: convert a hostile-validation receipt into a review write (plugin), then policy HvVerdictMapping [FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-005]

Actors: Operator, agent host (any of the nine), plugin hooks or tools, model. Precondition: workspace trusted (marker signature and health nonce verified). Basic flow: operator submits a prompt; on a prompt-hook or adapter host the hook classifies it as a user request, takes the turn-open lock, derives the nonce from the event (host binding table), asks the server to mint the requestId (the server opens the turn), and records the token as the host session's write target at once; on a bridge host (claude-code, claude-cowork) the arrival bridge mints from the transcript `enqueue` record (state `queued`) and the request becomes the write target at its `dequeue`, or at an `absorbed_mid_turn` removal (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009, -AC010); the request enters the stop ledger when it is delivered (at once on prompt-hook and adapter hosts; at its `dequeue` or `absorbed_mid_turn` removal on bridge hosts), never at mint; every verb the model invokes is bound automatically to the host session's write target at invocation start; model closes the turn. Actors: Operator, agent host (any of the nine), plugin hooks or tools, model. Precondition: workspace trusted (marker signature and health nonce verified). Basic flow: operator submits a prompt; on a prompt-hook or adapter host the hook classifies it as a user request, takes the turn-open lock, derives the nonce from the event (host binding table), asks the server to mint the requestId (the server opens the turn), and records the token as the host session's write target at once; on a bridge host (claude-code, claude-cowork) the arrival bridge mints from the transcript `enqueue` record (state `queued`) and the request becomes the write target at its `dequeue`, or at an `absorbed_mid_turn` removal (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009, -AC010); the request enters the stop ledger when it is delivered (at once on prompt-hook and adapter hosts; at its `dequeue` or `absorbed_mid_turn` removal on bridge hosts), never at mint; every verb the model invokes is bound automatically to the host session's write target at invocation start; model closes the turn. Alternate flows: the mint call is retried or replayed and returns the same requestId; a doubly registered hook delivers the event twice and both deliveries get the same requestId (only on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id or the bridge's single ordered source; on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails the host session closed under the equal-field rule, while a stored mint retry or failsafe drain reuses its nonce); the server is unreachable and a provisional `pending-<nonce>` turn is rebound on drain; an identical prompt sent again later is a new event and opens a second turn; background event is skipped (on a bridge host it keeps its queue position as an unminted system entry, so its `dequeue` delivers nothing); operator sends a message mid-turn, the arrival bridge mints its turn at enqueue without touching the running turn or the write target, the message is delivered (absorbed into the running turn, or dequeued) and from then on, while the earlier request is still open, an unqualified write is refused with `request_ambiguous` (D9) and the model names the requestId of each write; once the earlier request is closed, unqualified writes bind to the delivered request; the operator pulls a queued message back (`popAll`) before delivery, the request is withdrawn, and the stop gate asks the model to fail it; a verb without a host session key in a workspace with two live sessions is refused rather than guessed; a subagent's hooks fire and leave this session's turns unchanged; while two delivered requests are open an unqualified verb is refused with `request_ambiguous` and the model names the requestId (D9); on Copilot with more than one MCP prompt hook registered the hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and mints nothing (D11); on a host with no arrival mechanism every session-log verb reports `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6). type: request
payload:

  method: workflow.requirements.listFr
  params:

type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  result:

type: request

To retrieve a filtered list of functional requirements:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.listFr
  params:
    area: MCP
    status: in_progress
```

All params are optional; omit to return all FRs. The result contains an `items` array:

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  result:
    items:
      - id: FR-MCP-001
        title: Agent authentication
        description: System must authenticate AI agents via API key
        status: completed
        priority: critical
        area: MCP
        createdAt: 2026-03-01T10:00:00Z
        updatedAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z

```

590: UC-1 Log each user request as exactly one turn. Actors: Operator, agent host (any of the nine), plugin hooks or tools, model. Precondition: workspace trusted (marker signature and health nonce verified). Basic flow: operator submits a prompt; on a prompt-hook or adapter host the hook classifies it as a user request, takes the turn-open lock, derives the nonce from the event (host binding table), asks the server to mint the requestId (the server opens the turn), and records the token as the host session's write target at once; on a bridge host (claude-code, claude-cowork) the arrival bridge mints from the transcript `enqueue` record (state `queued`) and the request becomes the write target at its `dequeue`, or at an `absorbed_mid_turn` removal (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009, -AC010); the request enters the stop ledger when it is delivered (at once on prompt-hook and adapter hosts; at its `dequeue` or `absorbed_mid_turn` removal on bridge hosts), never at mint; every verb the model invokes is bound automatically to the host session's write target at invocation start; model closes the turn. Alternate flows: the mint call is retried or replayed and returns the same requestId; a doubly registered hook delivers the event twice and both deliveries get the same requestId (only on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id or the bridge's single ordered source; on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails the host session closed under the equal-field rule, while a stored mint retry or failsafe drain reuses its nonce); the server is unreachable and a provisional `pending-<nonce>` turn is rebound on drain; an identical prompt sent again later is a new event and opens a second turn; background event is skipped (on a bridge host it keeps its queue position as an unminted system entry, so its `dequeue` delivers nothing); operator sends a message mid-turn, the arrival bridge mints its turn at enqueue without touching the running turn or the write target, the message is delivered (absorbed into the running turn, or dequeued) and from then on, while the earlier request is still open, an unqualified write is refused with `request_ambiguous` (D9) and the model names the requestId of each write; once the earlier request is closed, unqualified writes bind to the delivered request; the operator pulls a queued message back (`popAll`) before delivery, the request is withdrawn, and the stop gate asks the model to fail it; a verb without a host session key in a workspace with two live sessions is refused rather than guessed; a subagent's hooks fire and leave this session's turns unchanged; while two delivered requests are open an unqualified verb is refused with `request_ambiguous` and the model names the requestId (D9); on Copilot with more than one MCP prompt hook registered the hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and mints nothing (D11); on a host with no arrival mechanism every session-log verb reports `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6). Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001, -002, -003, -007, -008; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-002, FR-MCP-REPL-010, FR-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-001.
