586: Related, unchanged (no edits; listed so reviewers can check): TEST-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001 (the AC first planned for it is TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC002, because its only evidence is a Build.Tests case); FR/TR/TEST-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-004 (replay of a `skipped_terminal` record must delete the failsafe, covered by A5 tests); FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001 and TR/TEST-MCP-SESSIONLOG-006 (planFile/todoId; pattern reused); FR-SUPPORT-015 / TR-SUPPORT-CORE-015 (additive merge; reviews replace whole records, documented as a single-valued section, not a collection); FR-SUPPORT-012, TR-MCP-SESSIONLOG-001/002/005; TR-MCP-SESSIONLOGSAN-001/002; FR-MCP-TRIAGEPLUGIN-001 (strengthened, no edit); FR-MCP-REPL-009, TR-MCP-REPL-010; TR-MCP-PLUGININT-001, TEST-MCP-PLUGININT-001 (generic outcome catalog gains skipped_terminal through FR-MCP-PLUGININT-001); TR-MCP-CLIENT-001 (new client body types registered); TR-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-002 (`Mcp:SessionLog` options section that hosts ReviewThresholds); FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-001..006 (separate subsystem; the turn `hostileReview` record is distinct and links by requestId); FR-MCP-143 (historical text); FR-MCP-USECASE-003/006/010 (coverage); TR-MCP-DB-006 (review section delete runs under the per-session lock). Pre-existing drift noted, not fixed here: FR-SUPPORT-013 `ac-3` and TEST-SUPPORT-010C-3 / TEST-SUPPORT-022 still describe PUT as 405 (triage).
587: 
588: ### Use cases (new, 9)
589: 
590: UC-1 Log each user request as exactly one turn. Actors: Operator, agent host (any of the nine), plugin hooks or tools, model. Precondition: workspace trusted (marker signature and health nonce verified). Basic flow: operator submits a prompt; on a prompt-hook or adapter host the hook classifies it as a user request, takes the turn-open lock, derives the nonce from the event (host binding table), asks the server to mint the requestId (the server opens the turn), and records the token as the host session's write target at once; on a bridge host (claude-code, claude-cowork) the arrival bridge mints from the transcript `enqueue` record (state `queued`) and the request becomes the write target at its `dequeue`, or at an `absorbed_mid_turn` removal (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009, -AC010); the request enters the stop ledger when it is delivered (at once on prompt-hook and adapter hosts; at its `dequeue` or `absorbed_mid_turn` removal on bridge hosts), never at mint; every verb the model invokes is bound automatically to the host session's write target at invocation start; model closes the turn. Alternate flows: the mint call is retried or replayed and returns the same requestId; a doubly registered hook delivers the event twice and both deliveries get the same requestId (only on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id or the bridge's single ordered source; on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails the host session closed under the equal-field rule, while a stored mint retry or failsafe drain reuses its nonce); the server is unreachable and a provisional `pending-<nonce>` turn is rebound on drain; an identical prompt sent again later is a new event and opens a second turn; background event is skipped (on a bridge host it keeps its queue position as an unminted system entry, so its `dequeue` delivers nothing); operator sends a message mid-turn, the arrival bridge mints its turn at enqueue without touching the running turn or the write target, the message is delivered (absorbed into the running turn, or dequeued) and from then on, while the earlier request is still open, an unqualified write is refused with `request_ambiguous` (D9) and the model names the requestId of each write; once the earlier request is closed, unqualified writes bind to the delivered request; the operator pulls a queued message back (`popAll`) before delivery, the request is withdrawn, and the stop gate asks the model to fail it; a verb without a host session key in a workspace with two live sessions is refused rather than guessed; a subagent's hooks fire and leave this session's turns unchanged; while two delivered requests are open an unqualified verb is refused with `request_ambiguous` and the model names the requestId (D9); on Copilot with more than one MCP prompt hook registered the hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and mints nothing (D11); on a host with no arrival mechanism every session-log verb reports `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6). Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001, -002, -003, -007, -008; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-002, FR-MCP-REPL-010, FR-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-001.
591: 
592: UC-2 Persist session-log writes with truthful receipts. Actors: model, plugin, server. Basic flow: model calls a verb; plugin persists; server returns per-turn outcome; plugin reports persisted only for created/merged. Alternate: target turn is terminal, server reports `skipped_terminal`, plugin reports `persisted:false`, exits non-zero, clears the failsafe; legacy server without outcomes yields `outcomeVerified:false`. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-003, FR-MCP-PLUGININT-001.
593: 
594: UC-3 Close every request turn before stopping. Actors: model, host Stop hook. Basic flow: model records actions/decisions (incl. via `designDecisions`) and closes each turn; Stop hook finds all closed with evidence and passes, clearing the ledger. Alternate: a turn is open (including one whose close the plugin refused for missing model evidence) or its most recent close was refused by the server's completion gate, the Stop hook blocks with the reason and the accepted remedy; a turn closed without evidence by another surface is only warned and never closes turns itself. Alternate: the host session failed closed under D6 (`unsupportedSince`) while a turn was open; the Stop hook blocks with the reduced remedy (only the missing model evidence, the missing `requestClass` from S8/S9, and the close call; the terminal reviews are judged at the drain), the model's evidence and close for that turn are captured in the plugin failsafe (reviews are refused and recorded after the drain through the original pair), the next Stop warns instead of blocking, and the next SessionStart drains the captured records with the turn's original pair through the trusted recovery flow. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005, -006; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-005, FR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001.
595: 
596: UC-4 Classify a request. Actors: model. Basic flow: model sets `requestClass` (Code, Docs, Chore) on its turn; an `Unstarted` hostile record flips to Unnecessary for Chore (and back if the class changes away while it is still Unnecessary), on in-progress turns only; records past Unstarted are never changed automatically. Alternate: invalid value rejected. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-006.
597: 
598: UC-5 Complete or fail a turn under the completion gate. Actors: model, server, server-internal writers. Basic flow: model completes; gate checks class and review statuses; turn completes. Alternate: gate unmet, 400 with missing items, turn stays in progress; fail requires only class; exempt origins bypass; the plugin, REPL, and McpAgent pre-checks only warn with the exact gate message and never refuse (the server gate is the only authority), and a server refusal is reported with the server's message and missing items; `canceled` is not gated. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002, -003, -004; updated FR-SUPPORT-013, FR-SUPPORT-014.
599: 
600: UC-6 Record an agent self-review. Actors: model via any of the nine plugins (on a host recorded `turn_logging_unsupported` every verb reports that code and no review is recorded). Basic flow: model records `agentReview` (Running, then scores); server derives Pass/Fail from thresholds and stamps them. Alternate: conflicting supplied status 422; invalid fields 400; review recorded after completion. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001, -002, -003, -006, -008, FR-SUPPORT-016 (new); updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGSAN-001.
601: 
602: UC-7 Record a hostile validation review with receipts. Actors: hostile reviewer (Codex CLI, gpt-6-astra, max), coordinator agent. Basic flow: at each HV point of "Execution organization" once its gates are green (D10), the coordinator writes the HV brief and launches the Codex reviewer; the runner records the request and response jsonl; the reviewer writes its markdown and JSON receipts and stores its entire result on its own session-log turn; from the Phase 4 live-check deploy on, the coordinator records `hostileReview` from the receipt (accuracy/completeness mapped, receipt paths set) and backfills the Phase 4 context verdicts by original pair before the phase-wide Phase 4 HV; for every HV point before that deploy, it records the verdict on the work package's coordinating turn (dialog and designDecisions with the receipt paths) and with `RecordValidationResultAsync`. Alternate: DISAGREE with passing scores recorded as Other with notes; missing receipt paths rejected; a run whose live model or effort is not gpt-6-astra/max is not accepted as HV; from the Phase 4 live-check deploy on, Code or Docs turns of a work package that completed before its HV carry `Other` "pending HV <gate>" and receive the verdict through `recordReview`, each addressed by its original (`sessionId`, `requestId`) pair (FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-002-AC002). Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-002, -005.
603: 
604: UC-8 Configure review pass thresholds. Actors: operator. Basic flow: operator sets thresholds per kind and score (or per instance); startup accepts them; new reviews derive with them and stamp them. Alternate: value outside [0,1] rejected. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-007.
605: 
606: UC-9 Read review scores losslessly. Actors: agents, client apps. Basic flow: a client reads a turn through REST, MCP, client, REPL, or a plugin and gets the exact decimal scores. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-004.

I want every unit of work request and respone defined. L94: 
L95: Write your own plugins to extend OpenCode.
L96: 
L97: Plugins allow you to extend OpenCode by hooking into various events and customizing behavior. You can create plugins to add new features, integrate with external services, or modify OpenCode’s default behavior.
L98: 
L99: For examples, check out the cite56†plugins created by the community.
L100: 
L101: * * *
L102: 
L103: ## cite39†Use a plugin L104: 
L105: There are two ways to load plugins.
L106: 
L107: * * *
L108: ### cite40†From local files L109: 
L110: Place JavaScript or TypeScript files in the plugin directory.
L111: 
L112:   * `.opencode/plugins/` - Project-level plugins
L113:   * `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` - Global plugins
L114: 
L115: Files in these directories are automatically loaded at startup.
L116: 
L117: * * *
L118: ### cite41†From npm L119: 
L120: Specify npm packages in your config file.
L121: 
L122: opencode.json
L123: 
L124:     `
L125: 
L126:     {
L127: 
L128:       "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
L129: 
L130:       "plugin": ["opencode-helicone-session", "opencode-wakatime", "@my-org/custom-plugin"]
L131: 
L132:     }
L133: 
L134:     `
L135: 
L136: Both regular and scoped npm packages are supported.
L137: 
L138: Browse available plugins in the cite56†ecosystem .
L139: 
L140: * * *
L141: ### cite42†How plugins are installed L142: 
L143: npm plugins are installed automatically using Bun at startup. Packages and their dependencies are cached in `~/.cache/opencode/node_modules/`.
L144: 
L145: Local plugins are loaded directly from the plugin directory. To use external packages, you must create a `package.json` within your config directory (see cite45†Dependencies ), or publish the plugin to npm and cite57†add it to your config .
L146: 
L147: * * *
L148: ### cite43†Load order L149: 
L150: Plugins are loaded from all sources and all hooks run in sequence. The load order is:
L151: 
L152:   1. Global config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`)
L153:   2. Project config (`opencode.json`)
L154:   3. Global plugin directory (`~/.config/opencode/plugins/`)
L155:   4. Project plugin directory (`.opencode/plugins/`)
L156: 
L157: Duplicate npm packages with the same name and version are loaded once. However, a local plugin and an npm plugin with similar names are both loaded separately.
L158: 
L159: * * *
L160: ## cite44†Create a plugin L161: 
L162: A plugin is a JavaScript/TypeScript module that exports one or more plugin functions. Each function receives a context object and returns a hooks object.
L163: 
L164: * * *
L165: ### cite45†Dependencies L166: 
L167: Local plugins and custom tools can use external npm packages. Add a `package.json` to your config directory with the dependencies you need.
L168: 
L169: .opencode/package.json
L170: 
L171:     `
L172: 
L173:     {
L174: 
L175:       "dependencies": {
L176: 
L177:         "shescape": "^2.1.0"
L178: 
L179:       }
L180: 
L181:     }
L182: 
L183:     `
L184: 
L185: OpenCode runs `bun install` at startup to install these. Your plugins and tools can then import them.
L186: .opencode/plugins/my-plugin.ts
L187: 
L188:     `
L189: 
L190:     import { escape } from "shescape"
L191: 
L192: 
L193: 
L194: 
L195:     export const MyPlugin = async (ctx) => {
L196: 
L197:       return {
L198: 
L199:         "tool.execute.before": async (input, output) => {
L200: 
L201:           if (input.tool === "bash") {
L202:

L204: 
L205:           }
L206: 
L207:         },
L208: 
L209:       }
L210: 
L211:     }
L212: 
L213:     `
L214:

L226: 
L227:

L232: 
L233:       }
L234: 
L235:     }
L236: 
L237:     `

# Agent Instructions

## Session Start

1. Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` in the repo root for the current API key and endpoints.
2. For specific operational steps (session bootstrap, session log turn workflow, and helper command sequence), follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.

On every subsequent user message:

1. Follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` for specific operational instructions.
2. Complete the user's request.

## Rules

1. `templates/prompt-templates.yaml` (`default-marker-prompt`) is the source of truth for specific agent instructions. `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` is the rendered runtime instruction set.
2. Keep this file focused on durable workspace policy and conventions; avoid duplicating marker-file operational procedures.
3. Use helper modules for session log and TODO operations. Do not make raw API calls.
4. Persist session log updates immediately after each meaningful change (turn creation, action append, decision, requirement, blocker, file/context update). Do not defer saves.
5. Capture rich turn detail: interpretation, response, status, actions (type/status/filePath), contextList, filesModified, designDecisions, requirementsDiscovered, blockers, and relevant processing dialog.
6. Follow workspace conventions in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` for build, test, and architecture guidance.
7. Use **only `pwsh.exe`** for shell commands and script execution; do not use `powershell.exe`.
8. When you need API schemas, module examples, or compliance rules, load them from `docs/context/` or use `context_search`.
9. Do not fabricate information. If you made a mistake, acknowledge it. Distinguish facts from speculation.
10. Prioritize correctness over speed. Do not ship code you have not verified compiles and is logically sound.
11. When writing session logs or other audit records, agents must identify themselves accurately using their real agent identity in Pascal-Case. Do not use placeholder, legacy, or misleading sourceType values.
12. Never edit YAML by appending, replacing, or removing text lines. Deserialize the complete document into an object, mutate the object, serialize it, and save it. Use `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` for PowerShell work.

## Byrd Test Gate

The canonical process is `docs/Development-Process-draft-v4.md`. To leave a Byrd implementation slice, the entire unit test suite for the current iteration and previous iterations must be completely passing. In this workspace, skipped tests are not passing tests: a validation gate requires zero failures and zero skips in the executed scope. Tests should directly track progress; deferred work belongs in MCP TODO/requirements state until that slice starts, not in skipped test placeholders.

## Where Things Live

- `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` — connection details, API key, workspace config (regenerated on server start)
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — build/test commands, architecture overview, coding conventions
- `docs/context/` — on-demand reference docs (schemas, module docs, compliance rules, action types)
- `docs/Project/` — requirements docs, TODO.yaml, mapping matrices
- `templates/` — prompt templates (loaded on demand)
- `tools/powershell/McpContext.psm1` — PowerShell module for context ingestion/query workflows
- `tools/powershell/McpContext.USER.md` — user-level guide for the McpContext module
- `tools/powershell/McpContext.AGENT.md` — agent workflow instructions for the McpContext module
- `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` — object-first YAML mutation helper for agents and plugin maintenance

## MCP Interaction via REPL Tools

Agents running inside `McpAgent` must use the 27 built-in tools instead of raw HTTP calls. See `docs/REPL-MIGRATION-GUIDE.md` for the full tool inventory and migration patterns.

Key rules:
- Use `mcp_session_*` tools for session log lifecycle (bootstrap, turns, history).
- Use `mcp_todo_*` tools for TODO CRUD (query, get, create, update, delete, plan, status, implementation).
- Use `mcp_requirements_*` tools for FR/TR/TEST queries.
- Use `mcp_client_invoke` for any sub-client method not covered by a dedicated tool (context search, GitHub, workspace, etc.).
- Do not make raw HTTP calls to `/qbrainai/*` endpoints when a tool is available.

## Context Loading by Task Type

- Agent Help: see marker `## Agent Help (QBrain.AI issues)` in `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`; API `/qbrainai/agent-help`
- Session logging → `docs/context/session-log-schema.md` + `docs/context/module-bootstrap.md`
- TODO management → `docs/context/todo-schema.md` + `docs/context/module-bootstrap.md`
- API integration → `docs/context/api-capabilities.md` (or `GET /swagger/v1/swagger.json`)
- Adding dependencies → `docs/context/compliance-rules.md`
- Logging actions → `docs/context/action-types.md`
- New to workspace → this file + `docs/context/api-capabilities.md`
- Migrating from raw API → `docs/REPL-MIGRATION-GUIDE.md`

## Agent Conduct

You represent the workspace owner. Your work directly reflects the owner's professional reputation.

### Honesty

- Do not fabricate information, capabilities, or results.
- Distinguish between facts, informed opinions, and speculation.
- Acknowledge mistakes immediately and correct them.

### Correctness

- Prioritize correctness over speed.
- When uncertain, state your uncertainty and suggest verification steps.
- Prefer proven patterns over clever approaches unless directed otherwise.
- All code must have XMLDocs. All public APIs must be documented.
- Follow DRY, SOLID, and existing project conventions.

### Decision Documentation

- Log every decision to the session log, including trivial ones.
- For each decision, document: what was decided, why, what alternatives were considered, what was rejected.
- Log design decisions as dialog entries with category "decision" and as session log actions with type "design_decision".

### Professional Representation

- Every interaction is audited via the session log.
- Every commit must be correct, clean, well-described, and complete.
- Log all commits as actions with type "commit" (SHA, branch, message, files).
- Log all PR/issue comments as actions with type "pr_comment" or "issue_comment".
- Always sign PR comments using the same signature convention as commits, identifying the actual authoring agent.

### Source Attribution

- Document all web sources in the session log as actions with type "web_reference" (URL, title, usage).
- Add source URLs to the turn's contextList array.
- Attribute external code in both the session log and code comments.

## Requirements Tracking

When you discover or agree on new requirements during a session:

1. Update the files in `docs/Project/`:
   - `Functional-Requirements.md` — append FR-MCP-* entries
   - `Technical-Requirements.md` — append TR-MCP-* entries
   - `TR-per-FR-Mapping.md` — append mapping rows
   - `Requirements-Matrix.md` — append status rows
   - `Testing-Requirements.md` — append TEST-MCP-* entries
2. Include the requirement ID in your session log turn's tags.
3. Capture requirements as they emerge. Do not defer to later.

## Design Decision Logging

When a design decision is made:

1. Log it as a session log dialog item with category "decision".
2. Include: the decision, alternatives considered, rationale, and affected requirements.
3. Add a session log action with type "design_decision".
4. If the decision affects existing code or requirements, note what needs updating.

## Session Continuity

At the start of every session:

1. Follow the session-start checklist in `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
2. Read `docs/Project/Requirements-Matrix.md` to understand project state.
3. If resuming interrupted work, review the last session's pending decisions.

At regular intervals during long sessions (~10 interactions):

1. Follow marker-file update cadence and session logging requirements from `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
2. Ensure all design decisions are captured.
3. Verify requirements docs are up to date.

## Glossary

- **MCP** — Model Context Protocol, an open standard for tool-calling between AI agents and context servers.
- **Workspace** — a project directory registered with the MCP server. All workspaces share a single port; use the `X-Workspace-Path` header to target a specific one.
- **Marker File** — the `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` file at each workspace root. Contains connection details, auth token, and agent prompt.
- **API Key** — a per-workspace cryptographic token that rotates on each server restart. Required for all `/qbrainai/*` REST endpoints.
- **Streamable HTTP** — the MCP wire protocol transport at `/mcp-transport`. Carries JSON-RPC tool calls over HTTP POST with streaming responses.
- **Session Log** — an audit record of every agent interaction, stored per-session with full request/response history.
- **Context Pack** — an ordered set of document chunks retrieved by semantic + full-text hybrid search, scoped to the workspace.
- **Tool Bucket** — a GitHub repository containing tool manifest files, similar to a Scoop package bucket.

## Response Formatting

- Do not use table-style output in responses.
- Use concise bullets or short paragraphs instead.

3711:## 8. Delivery: four execution phases and parallel domain coding
3712:
3713:Operator directive (2026-10-11, verbatim): "I want the implementation plan to be organized into requirements as a phase, interfaces and code stubs as a phase for the entire plan, test-driven development unit tests with mocks as a single phase, and then you can begin implementation coding in a domain-driven design breakdown so that agents can be run in parallel for the coding." The plan's section "Execution organization" is authoritative; this section describes it as architecture.
3714:
3715:### 8.1 Phase order
3716:
3717:```mermaid
3718:flowchart LR
3719:    PRE["Prerequisites: P0.1 baseline, REPL generateDocument fix, Nuke Test parameters, TestPluginCore, TestAgentPlugins, bats cases ported to Pester, Build.Tests out of MigrationIntegrationTests"] --> REQ["Phase 1 Requirements (the plan's P0 steps 1-9): every FR, TR, TEST, AC, mapping, use case, TODO"]
3720:    REQ --> DES["Phase 2 Interfaces and code stubs: every command, query, policy, seam, unregistered entity and configuration class, DTO, surface, plugin signature"]
3721:    DES --> TST["Phase 3 TDD unit tests with mocks: every unit test RED on stubs, then green on mocks with negative checks"]
3722:    TST --> IMP["Phase 4 Implementation: one coding agent per bounded context, in parallel"]
3723:    IMP --> VER["Integration, live checks on Linux and Windows, phase-wide HV, operator approval"]
3724:```
3725:
3726:Each arrow is crossed only after that phase's gates are green with zero failures and zero skips, its hostile validation (Codex gpt-6-astra max) returns AGREE at accuracy and completeness of at least 98 with every claim PASS, and the operator approves.
3727:
3728:### 8.2 What each phase delivers
3729:
3730:- Prerequisites: every pre-existing failure fixed under its own TODO (P0.1, including the Windows findings), the REPL `generateDocument` validator fix, the Nuke targets every later gate runs through (`Test --test-projects --test-filter`, `TestPluginCore`, `TestAgentPlugins`), and the port of every bats case to Pester (P0.1b; Pester is the only plugin test runner, operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."), and Build.Tests removed from `MigrationIntegrationTests` (P0.1c, TR-MCP-NUKE-014).
3731:- Phase 1, requirements (the plan's P0 steps 1-9): the whole catalog of Phases A, B, and C created in the requirement store from the plan text, the use cases, the feature matrix rows, and the phase and domain TODOs (`REQ-MERGEDPLAN-001`, `DESIGN-MERGEDPLAN-001`, `TEST-MERGEDPLAN-001`, one `IMPL-<CONTEXT>-001` per bounded context, `VERIFY-MERGEDPLAN-001`).
3732:- Phase 2, interfaces and code stubs: every command and query record with a handler stub, every policy and seam interface with a stub, every new entity class and its `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` as compiling, unregistered classes (no `DbSet`, no registration in `McpDbContext`, and no new property on an existing entity, because `McpDbContext.cs:301-308` ignores the pending-model-changes warning, so a registered model change without its migration would make queries select columns the database lacks and regress the existing tests that call `Migrate()`; the registered model change, the three migrations, and the S3 backfill belong to the Phase 4 context StorageSchema), every DTO and client mirror with JSON context registration, every controller route, MCP tool, client method, and REPL method (they only dispatch), every plugin function and tool signature, the options classes and `appsettings.yaml` sections, DI, and the golden contract files. Stubs return neutral values and never throw, so Phase 3 tests fail on assertions.
3733:- Phase 3, unit tests with mocks: every unit test the catalog names, written from the acceptance criteria, recorded RED against the stubs, then green against mocks with the oracle and mutant pattern and a recorded negative check each.
3734:- Phase 4, implementation: each bounded context replaces its stubs with the real implementation until its Phase 3 tests pass unchanged, adds its integration tests, and runs its gates; then the contexts merge in the rollout order and the integration gates, live checks, and phase-wide HV run.

4257:Relationship notes:
4258:
4259:- `SessionLog` to `SessionLogTurn` and every turn child are existing foreign keys; Phase B adds `SessionLogTurnReviewReason` as a new child of the turn (one row per reason, discriminated by `Kind`, ordered by `Ordinal`), and the review fields as columns on the turn row (one record per kind per turn, so no separate review table).
4260:- Phase A adds `SessionLogTurn.IngressNonce` with a unique filtered index per MCP session (WorkspaceId, SessionLogId, IngressNonce), and a second unique filtered index on (WorkspaceId, RequestId) where IngressNonce is set, so a server-minted `RequestId` is unique across the workspace's sessions; legacy rows keep their per-session uniqueness (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-006).
4261:- `AgentContextPackage` and `AgentResponse` refer to their turn by the root ids `SessionId` and `RequestId` (with `Agent` on the package), not by the turn's numeric `Id`, so packages and responses survive turn soft-delete and federation snapshots that renumber turn rows; the service validates the turn exists when a package is built (BuildAgentContextPackageCommand).
4262:- `AgentContextPackageItem.SourceRef`, `AgentContextRelationship.FromRef`/`ToRef`, and `AgentContextFinding.RelationshipId` are polymorphic or soft references resolved by kind in the service layer; staleness (EvaluateStalenessCommand) compares each reference's current hash with the stored `SourceSha256` or `ToSha256`.
4263:- `AgentResponse.SupersededByResponseId` is a self reference within one request; SupersedeAgentResponseCommand prevents cycles, and a `supersedes` row in `AgentContextRelationship` records the same link with its evidence.
4264:- `AgentContextProjection` has at most one row per response (key `ResponseId`); its `GraphRagDocumentId` is the id of the `ContextDocumentEntity` row (the `Documents` set, id `adhoc-<Guid>`) that `IGraphRagService.IngestTextAsync` creates with its `ContextChunkEntity` children (`src/QBrainAi.GraphRag/Services/GraphRagService.cs:348-372`), always in the workspace scope; removal deletes that document and its chunks (`IGraphRagService.DeleteDocumentAsync`). It never points at a knowledge-graph entity (`GraphEntity`, which stays a separate graph node) or at the global scope.
4265:- Requirement-family keys are composite (`WorkspaceId`, `Kind`, `Id`); TODO keys are (`WorkspaceId`, `Id`); agent-context keys are human-readable strings derived from the turn and session they belong to (`pkg-`, `rsp-`, `grd-`, `rel-`, `hvr-`, section 6.3); every child row of the new tables uses a `long` identity key.
4266:- `AgentContextHvRequest` names a range of turns of one MCP session (logical reference by `SessionId`); its items list the responses in that range when it was created; each model grade names the HV request that produced it (foreign key), and the request completes when no item stays `Pending` (each item `Graded`, or `Closed` because its response was rejected or superseded, section 6.3).

3711:## 8. Delivery: four execution phases and parallel domain coding
3712:
3713:Operator directive (2026-10-11, verbatim): "I want the implementation plan to be organized into requirements as a phase, interfaces and code stubs as a phase for the entire plan, test-driven development unit tests with mocks as a single phase, and then you can begin implementation coding in a domain-driven design breakdown so that agents can be run in parallel for the coding." The plan's section "Execution organization" is authoritative; this section describes it as architecture.
3714:
3715:### 8.1 Phase order
3716:
3717:```mermaid
3718:flowchart LR
3719:    PRE["Prerequisites: P0.1 baseline, REPL generateDocument fix, Nuke Test parameters, TestPluginCore, TestAgentPlugins, bats cases ported to Pester, Build.Tests out of MigrationIntegrationTests"] --> REQ["Phase 1 Requirements (the plan's P0 steps 1-9): every FR, TR, TEST, AC, mapping, use case, TODO"]
3720:    REQ --> DES["Phase 2 Interfaces and code stubs: every command, query, policy, seam, unregistered entity and configuration class, DTO, surface, plugin signature"]
3721:    DES --> TST["Phase 3 TDD unit tests with mocks: every unit test RED on stubs, then green on mocks with negative checks"]
3722:    TST --> IMP["Phase 4 Implementation: one coding agent per bounded context, in parallel"]
3723:    IMP --> VER["Integration, live checks on Linux and Windows, phase-wide HV, operator approval"]
3724:```
3725:
3726:Each arrow is crossed only after that phase's gates are green with zero failures and zero skips, its hostile validation (Codex gpt-6-astra max) returns AGREE at accuracy and completeness of at least 98 with every claim PASS, and the operator approves.
3727:
3728:### 8.2 What each phase delivers
3729:
3730:- Prerequisites: every pre-existing failure fixed under its own TODO (P0.1, including the Windows findings), the REPL `generateDocument` validator fix, the Nuke targets every later gate runs through (`Test --test-projects --test-filter`, `TestPluginCore`, `TestAgentPlugins`), and the port of every bats case to Pester (P0.1b; Pester is the only plugin test runner, operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."), and Build.Tests removed from `MigrationIntegrationTests` (P0.1c, TR-MCP-NUKE-014).
3731:- Phase 1, requirements (the plan's P0 steps 1-9): the whole catalog of Phases A, B, and C created in the requirement store from the plan text, the use cases, the feature matrix rows, and the phase and domain TODOs (`REQ-MERGEDPLAN-001`, `DESIGN-MERGEDPLAN-001`, `TEST-MERGEDPLAN-001`, one `IMPL-<CONTEXT>-001` per bounded context, `VERIFY-MERGEDPLAN-001`).
3732:- Phase 2, interfaces and code stubs: every command and query record with a handler stub, every policy and seam interface with a stub, every new entity class and its `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` as compiling, unregistered classes (no `DbSet`, no registration in `McpDbContext`, and no new property on an existing entity, because `McpDbContext.cs:301-308` ignores the pending-model-changes warning, so a registered model change without its migration would make queries select columns the database lacks and regress the existing tests that call `Migrate()`; the registered model change, the three migrations, and the S3 backfill belong to the Phase 4 context StorageSchema), every DTO and client mirror with JSON context registration, every controller route, MCP tool, client method, and REPL method (they only dispatch), every plugin function and tool signature, the options classes and `appsettings.yaml` sections, DI, and the golden contract files. Stubs return neutral values and never throw, so Phase 3 tests fail on assertions.
3733:- Phase 3, unit tests with mocks: every unit test the catalog names, written from the acceptance criteria, recorded RED against the stubs, then green against mocks with the oracle and mutant pattern and a recorded negative check each.
3734:- Phase 4, implementation: each bounded context replaces its stubs with the real implementation until its Phase 3 tests pass unchanged, adds its integration tests, and runs its gates; then the contexts merge in the rollout order and the integration gates, live checks, and phase-wide HV run.

4257:Relationship notes:
4258:
4259:- `SessionLog` to `SessionLogTurn` and every turn child are existing foreign keys; Phase B adds `SessionLogTurnReviewReason` as a new child of the turn (one row per reason, discriminated by `Kind`, ordered by `Ordinal`), and the review fields as columns on the turn row (one record per kind per turn, so no separate review table).
4260:- Phase A adds `SessionLogTurn.IngressNonce` with a unique filtered index per MCP session (WorkspaceId, SessionLogId, IngressNonce), and a second unique filtered index on (WorkspaceId, RequestId) where IngressNonce is set, so a server-minted `RequestId` is unique across the workspace's sessions; legacy rows keep their per-session uniqueness (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-006).
4261:- `AgentContextPackage` and `AgentResponse` refer to their turn by the root ids `SessionId` and `RequestId` (with `Agent` on the package), not by the turn's numeric `Id`, so packages and responses survive turn soft-delete and federation snapshots that renumber turn rows; the service validates the turn exists when a package is built (BuildAgentContextPackageCommand).
4262:- `AgentContextPackageItem.SourceRef`, `AgentContextRelationship.FromRef`/`ToRef`, and `AgentContextFinding.RelationshipId` are polymorphic or soft references resolved by kind in the service layer; staleness (EvaluateStalenessCommand) compares each reference's current hash with the stored `SourceSha256` or `ToSha256`.
4263:- `AgentResponse.SupersededByResponseId` is a self reference within one request; SupersedeAgentResponseCommand prevents cycles, and a `supersedes` row in `AgentContextRelationship` records the same link with its evidence.
4264:- `AgentContextProjection` has at most one row per response (key `ResponseId`); its `GraphRagDocumentId` is the id of the `ContextDocumentEntity` row (the `Documents` set, id `adhoc-<Guid>`) that `IGraphRagService.IngestTextAsync` creates with its `ContextChunkEntity` children (`src/QBrainAi.GraphRag/Services/GraphRagService.cs:348-372`), always in the workspace scope; removal deletes that document and its chunks (`IGraphRagService.DeleteDocumentAsync`). It never points at a knowledge-graph entity (`GraphEntity`, which stays a separate graph node) or at the global scope.
4265:- Requirement-family keys are composite (`WorkspaceId`, `Kind`, `Id`); TODO keys are (`WorkspaceId`, `Id`); agent-context keys are human-readable strings derived from the turn and session they belong to (`pkg-`, `rsp-`, `grd-`, `rel-`, `hvr-`, section 6.3); every child row of the new tables uses a `long` identity key.
4266:- `AgentContextHvRequest` names a range of turns of one MCP session (logical reference by `SessionId`); its items list the responses in that range when it was created; each model grade names the HV request that produced it (foreign key), and the request completes when no item stays `Pending` (each item `Graded`, or `Closed` because its response was rejected or superseded, section 6.3).

3711:## 8. Delivery: four execution phases and parallel domain coding
3712:
3713:Operator directive (2026-10-11, verbatim): "I want the implementation plan to be organized into requirements as a phase, interfaces and code stubs as a phase for the entire plan, test-driven development unit tests with mocks as a single phase, and then you can begin implementation coding in a domain-driven design breakdown so that agents can be run in parallel for the coding." The plan's section "Execution organization" is authoritative; this section describes it as architecture.
3714:
3715:### 8.1 Phase order
3716:
3717:```mermaid
3718:flowchart LR
3719:    PRE["Prerequisites: P0.1 baseline, REPL generateDocument fix, Nuke Test parameters, TestPluginCore, TestAgentPlugins, bats cases ported to Pester, Build.Tests out of MigrationIntegrationTests"] --> REQ["Phase 1 Requirements (the plan's P0 steps 1-9): every FR, TR, TEST, AC, mapping, use case, TODO"]
3720:    REQ --> DES["Phase 2 Interfaces and code stubs: every command, query, policy, seam, unregistered entity and configuration class, DTO, surface, plugin signature"]
3721:    DES --> TST["Phase 3 TDD unit tests with mocks: every unit test RED on stubs, then green on mocks with negative checks"]
3722:    TST --> IMP["Phase 4 Implementation: one coding agent per bounded context, in parallel"]
3723:    IMP --> VER["Integration, live checks on Linux and Windows, phase-wide HV, operator approval"]
3724:```
3725:
3726:Each arrow is crossed only after that phase's gates are green with zero failures and zero skips, its hostile validation (Codex gpt-6-astra max) returns AGREE at accuracy and completeness of at least 98 with every claim PASS, and the operator approves.
3727:
3728:### 8.2 What each phase delivers
3729:
3730:- Prerequisites: every pre-existing failure fixed under its own TODO (P0.1, including the Windows findings), the REPL `generateDocument` validator fix, the Nuke targets every later gate runs through (`Test --test-projects --test-filter`, `TestPluginCore`, `TestAgentPlugins`), and the port of every bats case to Pester (P0.1b; Pester is the only plugin test runner, operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."), and Build.Tests removed from `MigrationIntegrationTests` (P0.1c, TR-MCP-NUKE-014).
3731:- Phase 1, requirements (the plan's P0 steps 1-9): the whole catalog of Phases A, B, and C created in the requirement store from the plan text, the use cases, the feature matrix rows, and the phase and domain TODOs (`REQ-MERGEDPLAN-001`, `DESIGN-MERGEDPLAN-001`, `TEST-MERGEDPLAN-001`, one `IMPL-<CONTEXT>-001` per bounded context, `VERIFY-MERGEDPLAN-001`).
3732:- Phase 2, interfaces and code stubs: every command and query record with a handler stub, every policy and seam interface with a stub, every new entity class and its `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` as compiling, unregistered classes (no `DbSet`, no registration in `McpDbContext`, and no new property on an existing entity, because `McpDbContext.cs:301-308` ignores the pending-model-changes warning, so a registered model change without its migration would make queries select columns the database lacks and regress the existing tests that call `Migrate()`; the registered model change, the three migrations, and the S3 backfill belong to the Phase 4 context StorageSchema), every DTO and client mirror with JSON context registration, every controller route, MCP tool, client method, and REPL method (they only dispatch), every plugin function and tool signature, the options classes and `appsettings.yaml` sections, DI, and the golden contract files. Stubs return neutral values and never throw, so Phase 3 tests fail on assertions.
3733:- Phase 3, unit tests with mocks: every unit test the catalog names, written from the acceptance criteria, recorded RED against the stubs, then green against mocks with the oracle and mutant pattern and a recorded negative check each.
3734:- Phase 4, implementation: each bounded context replaces its stubs with the real implementation until its Phase 3 tests pass unchanged, adds its integration tests, and runs its gates; then the contexts merge in the rollout order and the integration gates, live checks, and phase-wide HV run.

4257:Relationship notes:
4258:
4259:- `SessionLog` to `SessionLogTurn` and every turn child are existing foreign keys; Phase B adds `SessionLogTurnReviewReason` as a new child of the turn (one row per reason, discriminated by `Kind`, ordered by `Ordinal`), and the review fields as columns on the turn row (one record per kind per turn, so no separate review table).
4260:- Phase A adds `SessionLogTurn.IngressNonce` with a unique filtered index per MCP session (WorkspaceId, SessionLogId, IngressNonce), and a second unique filtered index on (WorkspaceId, RequestId) where IngressNonce is set, so a server-minted `RequestId` is unique across the workspace's sessions; legacy rows keep their per-session uniqueness (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-006).
4261:- `AgentContextPackage` and `AgentResponse` refer to their turn by the root ids `SessionId` and `RequestId` (with `Agent` on the package), not by the turn's numeric `Id`, so packages and responses survive turn soft-delete and federation snapshots that renumber turn rows; the service validates the turn exists when a package is built (BuildAgentContextPackageCommand).
4262:- `AgentContextPackageItem.SourceRef`, `AgentContextRelationship.FromRef`/`ToRef`, and `AgentContextFinding.RelationshipId` are polymorphic or soft references resolved by kind in the service layer; staleness (EvaluateStalenessCommand) compares each reference's current hash with the stored `SourceSha256` or `ToSha256`.
4263:- `AgentResponse.SupersededByResponseId` is a self reference within one request; SupersedeAgentResponseCommand prevents cycles, and a `supersedes` row in `AgentContextRelationship` records the same link with its evidence.
4264:- `AgentContextProjection` has at most one row per response (key `ResponseId`); its `GraphRagDocumentId` is the id of the `ContextDocumentEntity` row (the `Documents` set, id `adhoc-<Guid>`) that `IGraphRagService.IngestTextAsync` creates with its `ContextChunkEntity` children (`src/QBrainAi.GraphRag/Services/GraphRagService.cs:348-372`), always in the workspace scope; removal deletes that document and its chunks (`IGraphRagService.DeleteDocumentAsync`). It never points at a knowledge-graph entity (`GraphEntity`, which stays a separate graph node) or at the global scope.
4265:- Requirement-family keys are composite (`WorkspaceId`, `Kind`, `Id`); TODO keys are (`WorkspaceId`, `Id`); agent-context keys are human-readable strings derived from the turn and session they belong to (`pkg-`, `rsp-`, `grd-`, `rel-`, `hvr-`, section 6.3); every child row of the new tables uses a `long` identity key.
4266:- `AgentContextHvRequest` names a range of turns of one MCP session (logical reference by `SessionId`); its items list the responses in that range when it was created; each model grade names the HV request that produced it (foreign key), and the request completes when no item stays `Pending` (each item `Graded`, or `Closed` because its response was rejected or superseded, section 6.3).

3711:## 8. Delivery: four execution phases and parallel domain coding
3712:
3713:Operator directive (2026-10-11, verbatim): "I want the implementation plan to be organized into requirements as a phase, interfaces and code stubs as a phase for the entire plan, test-driven development unit tests with mocks as a single phase, and then you can begin implementation coding in a domain-driven design breakdown so that agents can be run in parallel for the coding." The plan's section "Execution organization" is authoritative; this section describes it as architecture.
3714:
3715:### 8.1 Phase order
3716:
3717:```mermaid
3718:flowchart LR
3719:    PRE["Prerequisites: P0.1 baseline, REPL generateDocument fix, Nuke Test parameters, TestPluginCore, TestAgentPlugins, bats cases ported to Pester, Build.Tests out of MigrationIntegrationTests"] --> REQ["Phase 1 Requirements (the plan's P0 steps 1-9): every FR, TR, TEST, AC, mapping, use case, TODO"]
3720:    REQ --> DES["Phase 2 Interfaces and code stubs: every command, query, policy, seam, unregistered entity and configuration class, DTO, surface, plugin signature"]
3721:    DES --> TST["Phase 3 TDD unit tests with mocks: every unit test RED on stubs, then green on mocks with negative checks"]
3722:    TST --> IMP["Phase 4 Implementation: one coding agent per bounded context, in parallel"]
3723:    IMP --> VER["Integration, live checks on Linux and Windows, phase-wide HV, operator approval"]
3724:```
3725:
3726:Each arrow is crossed only after that phase's gates are green with zero failures and zero skips, its hostile validation (Codex gpt-6-astra max) returns AGREE at accuracy and completeness of at least 98 with every claim PASS, and the operator approves.
3727:
3728:### 8.2 What each phase delivers
3729:
3730:- Prerequisites: every pre-existing failure fixed under its own TODO (P0.1, including the Windows findings), the REPL `generateDocument` validator fix, the Nuke targets every later gate runs through (`Test --test-projects --test-filter`, `TestPluginCore`, `TestAgentPlugins`), and the port of every bats case to Pester (P0.1b; Pester is the only plugin test runner, operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."), and Build.Tests removed from `MigrationIntegrationTests` (P0.1c, TR-MCP-NUKE-014).
3731:- Phase 1, requirements (the plan's P0 steps 1-9): the whole catalog of Phases A, B, and C created in the requirement store from the plan text, the use cases, the feature matrix rows, and the phase and domain TODOs (`REQ-MERGEDPLAN-001`, `DESIGN-MERGEDPLAN-001`, `TEST-MERGEDPLAN-001`, one `IMPL-<CONTEXT>-001` per bounded context, `VERIFY-MERGEDPLAN-001`).
3732:- Phase 2, interfaces and code stubs: every command and query record with a handler stub, every policy and seam interface with a stub, every new entity class and its `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` as compiling, unregistered classes (no `DbSet`, no registration in `McpDbContext`, and no new property on an existing entity, because `McpDbContext.cs:301-308` ignores the pending-model-changes warning, so a registered model change without its migration would make queries select columns the database lacks and regress the existing tests that call `Migrate()`; the registered model change, the three migrations, and the S3 backfill belong to the Phase 4 context StorageSchema), every DTO and client mirror with JSON context registration, every controller route, MCP tool, client method, and REPL method (they only dispatch), every plugin function and tool signature, the options classes and `appsettings.yaml` sections, DI, and the golden contract files. Stubs return neutral values and never throw, so Phase 3 tests fail on assertions.
3733:- Phase 3, unit tests with mocks: every unit test the catalog names, written from the acceptance criteria, recorded RED against the stubs, then green against mocks with the oracle and mutant pattern and a recorded negative check each.
3734:- Phase 4, implementation: each bounded context replaces its stubs with the real implementation until its Phase 3 tests pass unchanged, adds its integration tests, and runs its gates; then the contexts merge in the rollout order and the integration gates, live checks, and phase-wide HV run.

3732:- Phase 2, interfaces and code stubs: every command and query record with a handler stub, every policy and seam interface with a stub, every new entity class and its `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` as compiling, unregistered classes (no `DbSet`, no registration in `McpDbContext`, and no new property on an existing entity, because `McpDbContext.cs:301-308` ignores the pending-model-changes warning, so a registered model change without its migration would make queries select columns the database lacks and regress the existing tests that call `Migrate()`; the registered model change, the three migrations, and the S3 backfill belong to the Phase 4 context StorageSchema), every DTO and client mirror with JSON context registration, every controller route, MCP tool, client method, and REPL method (they only dispatch), every plugin function and tool signature, the options classes and `appsettings.yaml` sections, DI, and the golden contract files. 3838:### 8.5 Rollout and rollback
3839:
3840:- Merge and deploy order: StorageSchema, SessionTurnLogging, TurnReviews without the CompletionGate enforcement change set, ContextPackages, ResponsesAndTrust, ContextGraph, ReplAndAgents; deploy the server (agent context Mode `Off`); merge PluginCorePowerShell, BuildTooling; sync all nine plugins once at one explicit version (`./build.ps1 SyncAgentPlugins --agent-plugin-parent /home/sharpninja/github --plugin-version 1.119.0`, which carries the Phase A, B, and C plugin work together; the installed-equals-synced step and the operator's codex hook trust follow, and a same-version re-sync, which refreshes content and never bumps the version, runs only when a later Phase 4 fix changes `plugins/core/lib-ps`); merge HostPluginAdoption (then `MAINT-LIBSHRETIRE-001`, and once Codex ACKs the 2026-10-12 PowerShell-only CONTRACT entry or the operator resolves it `MAINT-LIBNODERETIRE-001`); merge and deploy the CompletionGate enforcement change set; Documentation; then the integration checks.
3841:- Mode `Pilot` only on the operator's instruction; the pilot report goes to the operator; `Stateless` as a default is a later operator decision.
3842:- Server deploys run through the Nuke `UpdateService` target with operator approval; releases use Octopus only. Rollback: Mode `Off` stops agent-context behavior without a deploy; migrations roll back only through their tested Down.

3844:### 8.6 End-to-end verification
3845:
3846:- Turn logging and reviews: the live checks of the plan's "End-to-end verification" section.
3847:- Agent context with Mode `Pilot` on LAB-OMARCHY and PAYTON-LEGION2: a delivered request builds one package with the request's root ids; replay reports `identical: true`; an over-budget fixture refuses the prompt with `agent_context_budget_exceeded` and closes the turn `canceled`; a submitted response passes the deterministic grade, an HV request covering its turn is created, the HV agent records a passing model grade with verified receipts, and the response becomes `Trusted`; a later package includes it as a prior response; changing a file it depends on makes it `Stale`; with GraphRAG disabled retrieval reports `graphrag_disabled` and answers from the relational path; with GraphRAG enabled the trusted response is projected and a rejected one removed.

docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:6:This document describes the whole merged plan as architecture: the components, the data each part owns, every unit of work with its request, response, and error contract, one complete activity diagram per unit of work, and sequence diagrams for submitting each request type and processing each response. 51:Common rules: string keys `[StringLength(128)]`, human-readable and derived from the records they belong to (formats per entity below). Bounded readable keys: a key is `<prefix><parentId><tail>` when that is at most 128 characters; otherwise the embedded parent id is shortened to its first `128 - length(prefix) - length(tail) - 13` characters followed by `-` and the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the full parent id, so keys stay readable, deterministic, and distinct for distinct parents; the complete parent ids are always stored in their own root-id columns, which keep the live length of 256 (`SessionLogEntity.SessionId` and `SessionLogTurnEntity.RequestId` allow 256), so no root id is ever truncated (`AgentContextKeys_MaxLengthRootIds_FitAndStayDistinct` on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; `AgentContextKeys_ShortRootIds_KeepFullReadableForm`); a sequence suffix `<nn>` (two digits, from 01) is allocated as one more than the highest existing suffix for that prefix, and a unique-index violation from a concurrent insert retries with the next suffix (at most five times, then 409 `conflict`); child rows use `long` identity keys; every entity has `[Required][StringLength(1024)] WorkspaceId` with the named `Workspace` query filter and `StampWorkspaceId` on add; timestamps are `DateTimeOffset` named `*Utc`; decimals are `HasPrecision(29, 28)`; list-valued data is stored in 4NF child tables; idempotency comes from unique indexes (the store has no concurrency tokens). Per-response serialization: every write that changes a response's grades or status (RunDeterministicGradeCommand and RecordModelGradeCommand with DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand, RejectAgentResponseCommand, SupersedeAgentResponseCommand, and EvaluateStalenessCommand) runs in one transaction at `IsolationLevel.Serializable` (the convention of `SessionLogService.cs:156`) whose first statement increments that response's `StatusVersion`, so every such operation on one response takes the row's write lock first and they serialize in commit order on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; a serialization failure or deadlock (PostgreSQL 40001 or 40P01, SQL Server 1205, SQLite busy) rolls the whole operation back and retries it from the start, at most three times, then returns 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` (`Trust_ForcedInterleaving_DeterministicFailVsModelPass_NeverTrustedOnSupersededGrade`, `Trust_ForcedInterleaving_RejectVsGrade_RejectedNeverRevived`, each on the three providers). Migrations `<yyyyMMddHHmmss>_AddAgentContext` are generated for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server with the existing `dotnet ef migrations add` procedure.

51:Common rules: string keys `[StringLength(128)]`, human-readable and derived from the records they belong to (formats per entity below). Bounded readable keys: a key is `<prefix><parentId><tail>` when that is at most 128 characters; otherwise the embedded parent id is shortened to its first `128 - length(prefix) - length(tail) - 13` characters followed by `-` and the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the full parent id, so keys stay readable, deterministic, and distinct for distinct parents; the complete parent ids are always stored in their own root-id columns, which keep the live length of 256 (`SessionLogEntity.SessionId` and `SessionLogTurnEntity.RequestId` allow 256), so no root id is ever truncated (`AgentContextKeys_MaxLengthRootIds_FitAndStayDistinct` on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; `AgentContextKeys_ShortRootIds_KeepFullReadableForm`); a sequence suffix `<nn>` (two digits, from 01) is allocated as one more than the highest existing suffix for that prefix, and a unique-index violation from a concurrent insert retries with the next suffix (at most five times, then 409 `conflict`); child rows use `long` identity keys; every entity has `[Required][StringLength(1024)] WorkspaceId` with the named `Workspace` query filter and `StampWorkspaceId` on add; timestamps are `DateTimeOffset` named `*Utc`; decimals are `HasPrecision(29, 28)`; list-valued data is stored in 4NF child tables; idempotency comes from unique indexes (the store has no concurrency tokens). Per-response serialization: every write that changes a response's grades or status (RunDeterministicGradeCommand and RecordModelGradeCommand with DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand, RejectAgentResponseCommand, SupersedeAgentResponseCommand, and EvaluateStalenessCommand) runs in one transaction at `IsolationLevel.Serializable` (the convention of `SessionLogService.cs:156`) whose first statement increments that response's `StatusVersion`, so every such operation on one response takes the row's write lock first and they serialize in commit order on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; a serialization failure or deadlock (PostgreSQL 40001 or 40P01, SQL Server 1205, SQLite busy) rolls the whole operation back and retries it from the start, at most three times, then returns 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` (`Trust_ForcedInterleaving_DeterministicFailVsModelPass_NeverTrustedOnSupersededGrade`, `Trust_ForcedInterleaving_RejectVsGrade_RejectedNeverRevived`, each on the three providers). Migrations `<yyyyMMddHHmmss>_AddAgentContext` are generated for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server with the existing `dotnet ef migrations add` procedure.

51:Common rules: string keys `[StringLength(128)]`, human-readable and derived from the records they belong to (formats per entity below). Bounded readable keys: a key is `<prefix><parentId><tail>` when that is at most 128 characters; otherwise the embedded parent id is shortened to its first `128 - length(prefix) - length(tail) - 13` characters followed by `-` and the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the full parent id, so keys stay readable, deterministic, and distinct for distinct parents; the complete parent ids are always stored in their own root-id columns, which keep the live length of 256 (`SessionLogEntity.SessionId` and `SessionLogTurnEntity.RequestId` allow 256), so no root id is ever truncated (`AgentContextKeys_MaxLengthRootIds_FitAndStayDistinct` on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; `AgentContextKeys_ShortRootIds_KeepFullReadableForm`); a sequence suffix `<nn>` (two digits, from 01) is allocated as one more than the highest existing suffix for that prefix, and a unique-index violation from a concurrent insert retries with the next suffix (at most five times, then 409 `conflict`); child rows use `long` identity keys; every entity has `[Required][StringLength(1024)] WorkspaceId` with the named `Workspace` query filter and `StampWorkspaceId` on add; timestamps are `DateTimeOffset` named `*Utc`; decimals are `HasPrecision(29, 28)`; list-valued data is stored in 4NF child tables; idempotency comes from unique indexes (the store has no concurrency tokens). Per-response serialization: every write that changes a response's grades or status (RunDeterministicGradeCommand and RecordModelGradeCommand with DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand, RejectAgentResponseCommand, SupersedeAgentResponseCommand, and EvaluateStalenessCommand) runs in one transaction at `IsolationLevel.Serializable` (the convention of `SessionLogService.cs:156`) whose first statement increments that response's `StatusVersion`, so every such operation on one response takes the row's write lock first and they serialize in commit order on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; a serialization failure or deadlock (PostgreSQL 40001 or 40P01, SQL Server 1205, SQLite busy) rolls the whole operation back and retries it from the start, at most three times, then returns 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` (`Trust_ForcedInterleaving_DeterministicFailVsModelPass_NeverTrustedOnSupersededGrade`, `Trust_ForcedInterleaving_RejectVsGrade_RejectedNeverRevived`, each on the three providers). Migrations `<yyyyMMddHHmmss>_AddAgentContext` are generated for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server with the existing `dotnet ef migrations add` procedure.

Bounded readable keys: a key is `<prefix><parentId><tail>` when that is at most 128 characters; otherwise the embedded parent id is shortened to its first `128 - length(prefix) - length(tail) - 13` characters followed by `-` and the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the full parent id, so keys stay readable, deterministic, and distinct for distinct parents; the complete parent ids are always stored in their own root-id columns, which keep the live length of 256 (`SessionLogEntity.SessionId` and `SessionLogTurnEntity.RequestId` allow 256), so no root id is ever truncated (`AgentContextKeys_MaxLengthRootIds_FitAndStayDistinct` on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; `AgentContextKeys_ShortRootIds_KeepFullReadableForm`); a sequence suffix `<nn>` (two digits, from 01) is allocated as one more than the highest existing suffix for that prefix, and a unique-index violation from a concurrent insert retries with the next suffix (at most five times, then 409 `conflict`); child rows use `long` identity keys; every entity has `[Required][StringLength(1024)] WorkspaceId` with the named `Workspace` query filter and `StampWorkspaceId` on add; timestamps are `DateTimeOffset` named `*Utc`; decimals are `HasPrecision(29, 28)`; list-valued data is stored in 4NF child tables; idempotency comes from unique indexes (the store has no concurrency tokens). 226:- HV points are those of "Execution organization" (each prerequisite, the end of Phases 1, 2, and 3, each bounded context at the end of its Phase 4 work package, and the phase-wide Phase 4 HV); they replace the approved pre-merge per-slice schedule (HV-P0 at P0's end, HV-A1..HV-A9, HV-S1..HV-S11, and the phase-wide HV-A and HV-B), and "HV-P0" below names the Phase 1 HV. Every work package ends with its own HV once its gates are green (D10). Turns of a Code or Docs work package that complete before its HV lands (operator confirmed this interpretation of D10 on 2026-10-09: "agree") record `hostileReview` status `Other` with `otherNotes` "pending HV <gate>" from the first deploy whose server stores review records, the Phase 4 live-check deploy; when the HV lands, its verdict, mapped as FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-005-AC002 states (server-derived Pass or Fail from the scores, or `Other` with `otherNotes` naming the failed claims when a DISAGREE has scores that would derive Pass), with both receipt paths is recorded with `recordReview` onto every turn of that work package, each addressed by its original (`sessionId`, `requestId`) pair (FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-002-AC002) (reviews stay writable on completed turns), and the HV brief lists those turns. Before that deploy, every HV point (the prerequisites, Phases 1-3, and the Phase 4 context HVs, which run before their contexts merge) records its verdict on its coordinating turn (dialog and designDecisions with the receipt paths) and with `RecordValidationResultAsync`, and its TODO moves to Complete on its HV pass. After that deploy, and before the phase-wide Phase 4 HV reviewer is launched, the Phase 4 context verdicts are recorded with `recordReview` onto every turn of those contexts by original pair (FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-002-AC002), the phase-wide brief lists those turns with its own, and `VERIFY-MERGEDPLAN-001` moves to Complete only after `client.SessionLog.QueryAsync` shows every turn listed in that brief carrying its verdict; an interrupted backfill is re-run (identical writes are no-ops).
227:- At each HV point, once its gates are green, push the worktree branch (and the branch of each plugin repo the work package changed). Write the HV brief: the claims (with commands, paths, test counts, SHAs, session turn ids), the untrusted implementer receipt, the acceptance rule, mandatory surfaces A-D, the add-profile first action, the review-only scope, and the receipt paths.
228:- Launch the reviewer with `codex exec -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort="max" --sandbox workspace-write -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true -C <worktree> --json -`, brief on stdin. The reviewer is review-only (it writes only under `docs/receipts/hv/` and to its own MCP session-log turn) and returns claim-by-claim PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN, `OverallVerdict`, accuracy, completeness, findings, and a `=== VERDICT JSON ===` block. The implementing agent writes the brief and launches the run; it never edits the reviewer's output or verdict. Verify the live model and effort from the Codex session rollout (`turn_context` with `model=gpt-6-astra`, `effort=max`); a run on any other model or effort is not an HV. Review time is unbounded (operator, 2026-10-12: "Do not bound review time"): no timeout, kill, deadline, or wait limit on the reviewer, and no expected duration in a brief; the implementer checks the response stream until `turn.completed` arrives.
229:- Receipts: the runner writes `docs/receipts/hv/<utc>-<gate>.request.jsonl` (a meta object with the launch command, model, effort, head SHA, and brief SHA-256, plus the full brief body; built from PowerShell objects with `ConvertTo-Json -Compress`) and `.response.jsonl` (the reviewer's complete `--json` event stream), and, after the reviewer completes, `.rollout.jsonl` (a copy of the completed reviewer thread's Codex rollout file, which records its runtime `turn_context`; the agent-context `runtime_identity` check reads it). The reviewer writes `hostile-validator-<gate>-<utc>.md` and `.json`. All are committed on the branch only after every marker key value and every `apiKey`, `api_key`, or `X-Api-Key` value of 20 or more characters in them is replaced with `[REDACTED:api-key]`, no other byte changing, and a scan against the current markers' keys finds no match (the repository is public, and the reviewer reads the markers). Store the complete verdict in the MCP session log on the turn that launched the HV (the work package's coordinating turn) (ordered dialog parts that concatenate byte for byte to the markdown receipt, plus designDecisions, the jsonl paths, and the Codex rollout path); the reviewer also stores it on its own turn, through the supported Codex plugin wrapper (manual `workflow.sessionlog.*` verbs when hooks do not mint), and reads it back; this is mandatory at every HV point: an HV whose reviewer turn cannot be created, populated, completed, and read back is incomplete, its work package stays open, and the coordinator's turn never substitutes for it. From the deploy that carries the CompletionGate enforcement change set (in the Phase 4 rollout order, and every later deploy), the reviewer's own turn meets that gate like any other: the HV brief has the reviewer, through the installed 1.119.0 Codex plugin, set its turn's `requestClass` to `Chore` (a review writes receipts, not product code or documentation, so its hostile record becomes `Unnecessary`) and record its `agentReview` as `Other` with `otherNotes` naming its verdict receipt (a review turn's self-review is its own verdict), before it completes the turn. Because codex reports `turn_logging_unsupported` after a refresh of its installed copy (the installed-equals-synced step, Per-plugin changes) changes its hook definition, until the operator trusts that definition and the codex live assertion passes (host binding table), that trust step and the assertion run after each such refresh and before the next HV reviewer is launched; if they cannot pass, the HV is not launched and the operator is shown the blocker. From the Phase 4 live-check deploy (the per-turn recording start above), also record it with `workflow.sessionlog.recordReview kind: hostile` (with `requestJsonlPath`/`responseJsonlPath`).

On DISAGREE or any other non-pass (including AGREE with a FAIL or UNKNOWN claim): display every FAIL/UNKNOWN to the operator, fix on the branch, push, and launch a new Codex round whose brief re-attacks the prior receipt; the work package stays open (and, at a phase-end HV, its phase).

51:Common rules: string keys `[StringLength(128)]`, human-readable and derived from the records they belong to (formats per entity below). Bounded readable keys: a key is `<prefix><parentId><tail>` when that is at most 128 characters; otherwise the embedded parent id is shortened to its first `128 - length(prefix) - length(tail) - 13` characters followed by `-` and the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the full parent id, so keys stay readable, deterministic, and distinct for distinct parents; the complete parent ids are always stored in their own root-id columns, which keep the live length of 256 (`SessionLogEntity.SessionId` and `SessionLogTurnEntity.RequestId` allow 256), so no root id is ever truncated (`AgentContextKeys_MaxLengthRootIds_FitAndStayDistinct` on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; `AgentContextKeys_ShortRootIds_KeepFullReadableForm`); a sequence suffix `<nn>` (two digits, from 01) is allocated as one more than the highest existing suffix for that prefix, and a unique-index violation from a concurrent insert retries with the next suffix (at most five times, then 409 `conflict`); child rows use `long` identity keys; every entity has `[Required][StringLength(1024)] WorkspaceId` with the named `Workspace` query filter and `StampWorkspaceId` on add; timestamps are `DateTimeOffset` named `*Utc`; decimals are `HasPrecision(29, 28)`; list-valued data is stored in 4NF child tables; idempotency comes from unique indexes (the store has no concurrency tokens). Per-response serialization: every write that changes a response's grades or status (RunDeterministicGradeCommand and RecordModelGradeCommand with DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand, RejectAgentResponseCommand, SupersedeAgentResponseCommand, and EvaluateStalenessCommand) runs in one transaction at `IsolationLevel.Serializable` (the convention of `SessionLogService.cs:156`) whose first statement increments that response's `StatusVersion`, so every such operation on one response takes the row's write lock first and they serialize in commit order on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; a serialization failure or deadlock (PostgreSQL 40001 or 40P01, SQL Server 1205, SQLite busy) rolls the whole operation back and retries it from the start, at most three times, then returns 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` (`Trust_ForcedInterleaving_DeterministicFailVsModelPass_NeverTrustedOnSupersededGrade`, `Trust_ForcedInterleaving_RejectVsGrade_RejectedNeverRevived`, each on the three providers).
